providers.name: Teamtailor
providers.description: Teamtailor is an applicant tracking system (ATS) and employer branding platform that helps companies attract, engage, and hire candidates with customizable career sites, recruitment workflows, candidate communications, and analytics. The platform supports collaborative hiring, GDPR compliance, and a marketplace of integrations. Teamtailor's API follows the JSON:API specification with regional base URLs and uses token-based authentication with Public, Internal, and Admin key permission levels.

providers.name: Braid Social
providers.description: Braid Social, Inc. is a venture-backed startup that has run two products under the Braid name. It launched as a creator-economy, direct-to-fan engagement platform — founded by former Facebook product designer Matthew Cahill and software engineer Chris Piro — letting creators build customizable landing pages that consolidated their work across the web (blog posts, videos, podcasts, and commerce links), collect fan phone numbers, and reach followers directly through SMS, push notifications, and mailing lists, with link tracking and cross-platform analytics. It raised a $6.8M seed round in August 2023 led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) with Initialized Capital. The original domain braid.ai is now a domain-for-sale listing at atom.com and braid.social no longer resolves. The same legal entity now ships "Braid Teams" at trybraid.io (mirrored at braidsocial.com) — an AI-powered employee-engagement copilot that runs inside Slack, automating icebreakers, games, polls, events, reminders, leaderboards, and engagement reporting for distributed teams, on a free / $5-per-user Premium / contact-us Enterprise plan. Braid Teams is a Slack-app product with no public developer program: no developer portal, no documentation, no OpenAPI, no SDKs, and no GitHub organization. The only machine surface is the private application backend at core.trybraid.io, which answers {"status":"ok"} at its root and 404s every spec, docs and /.well-known/ path. The homepage states the product is "Currently not accepting new users" and the Slack install endpoint returns HTTP 500.

providers.name: Ellis
providers.description: Ellis is a modern business immigration platform and law firm that helps company People and HR teams secure U.S. work visas and green cards for skilled talent. The platform combines licensed immigration attorneys with software for centralized case management, document storage, status tracking, and program analytics, covering employment-based visas (H-1B, TN, O-1, L-1, J-1, E-1/E-2, E-3), green cards (EB-1A, EB-2 NIW, EB-2/EB-3 PERM), and naturalization. Ellis is a Kindred Ventures portfolio company. This API Evangelist profile was enriched from the company's public web surface; Ellis publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable artifacts at this time.

providers.name: Meritfirst
providers.description: MeritFirst is a skills-based hiring platform that replaces resume- and credential-based recruiting with practical, real-world assessments. Candidates prove their craft through work samples (Build, Try, Get Seen) and companies evaluate and match them on demonstrated ability rather than pedigree. MeritFirst exposes a hosted, authenticated Model Context Protocol (MCP) server so agents and tools can manage assessments, review candidates, and analyze hiring data. Backed by 8VC and Slow Ventures.

providers.name: Back
providers.description: Back is a Berlin-based employee experience and internal service platform that gives HR, IT, Finance, and Office teams one place to receive, automate, and resolve employee requests. It brings conversations from Slack, Microsoft Teams, and email into a single shared inbox, answers common questions with a self-service knowledge chatbot, and automates lifecycle journeys such as onboarding, offboarding, and leave with approvals, forms, and integrations. Founded in 2018 and backed by Point Nine and Seedcamp, Back is used by companies including Loom, Netlify, Choco, Pleo, Marley Spoon, and Statista. This profile was surfaced as a VC portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Back offers an API for custom integrations on select plans, but publishes no public developer portal, OpenAPI, or reference at time of enrichment.

providers.name: JobAdder
providers.description: JobAdder is a cloud-based recruitment and applicant tracking platform used by staffing agencies and in-house talent acquisition teams to manage jobs, candidates, placements, and client relationships. The platform offers a comprehensive REST API that exposes recruitment workflows including job posting, candidate search, application tracking, and analytics. The JobAdder API uses OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow with region-specific base URLs returned in the token response.

providers.name: Jobvite
providers.description: Jobvite, part of Employ Inc., is an applicant tracking system (ATS) and recruiting platform that helps enterprises source, hire, and onboard talent. The platform combines candidate relationship management, recruitment marketing, branded career sites, and onboarding workflows. Jobvite provides REST APIs that facilitate real-time data exchange in JSON for candidate records, requisitions, applications, and the Onboard New Hire endpoint.

providers.name: Bambee
providers.description: Bambee is an outsourced human-resources platform for American small and mid-sized businesses. Every membership pairs the company with a dedicated HR manager who audits existing HR practices, drafts compliant policies and employee handbooks, and guides owners through hiring, onboarding, corrective action, and terminations. Bambee also offers guided payroll and staff training, positioning itself as an all-in-one HR compliance solution that starts at a low monthly membership. The company is backed by QED Investors and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile. Bambee does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs; this record captures its public web and security surface.

providers.name: Blomma
providers.description: Blomma is an AI-powered career coaching platform that pairs artificial intelligence with emotional intelligence to act as a private thinking partner for professionals. Through chat-based coaching, guided reflection, goal-setting with built-in accountability, a personal journal, and a growth dashboard, Blomma helps founders, people leaders, and ambitious professionals turn abstract aspirations into concrete, trackable goals, and can personalize coaching from uploaded performance reviews and development plans. It is delivered as a consumer subscription through web and mobile apps, with custom team plans for organizations, and does not currently expose a public developer API.

providers.name: Bolster
providers.description: Bolster is an executive search and recruiting platform that pairs experienced recruiters with an AI-powered talent platform to place full-time executives, board members, and fractional or interim leaders for high-growth companies, startups, and venture capital firms. Bolster emphasizes speed (typically five days to a first interview), transparent flat-fee pricing, and a data-driven approach informed by analysis of more than 280,000 executives across 30,000+ companies, with 350+ placements and a 40% repeat-client rate. It is backed by Union Square Ventures.

providers.name: CLAP
providers.description: CLAP (주식회사 디웨일 / Dwhale Inc.) is a South Korean SaaS company offering an AI-powered, customizable performance management platform for enterprises. It covers the full performance lifecycle — multi-rater evaluations and calibration, OKR-style goal setting and alignment, continuous feedback and 1-on-1 meetings, and CLAP AI for diagnostics, feedback drafting, and automation — with tailored reporting and tool integrations. CLAP serves 1,000+ companies and claims to cut the HR time spent on performance management by up to 80%. The company is headquartered in Gangnam, Seoul, and is a portfolio company of 500 Global. CLAP publishes no public API or developer portal; this profile captures its identity and web properties.

providers.name: hampr
providers.description: hampr is an app-based, on-demand laundry pickup and delivery service founded by Laurel Hess and backed by Techstars. Members bag their dirty laundry, tap the hampr mobile app, and a local independent "washr" collects, professionally washes, dries, folds, and returns it to their door within 24 hours at flat-rate per-load pricing with free pickup and delivery. hampr operates across 16+ US states with 1,500+ washrs, 11,000+ members, and 300,000+ loads completed, and also runs hampr for business, a commercial laundry solution for salons, spas, gyms, and short-term rentals. This profile was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio lead and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; hampr is a consumer/commercial mobile service and publishes no public developer API.

providers.name: Helpling
providers.description: Helpling is an online marketplace that connects households with vetted, insured independent cleaners for on-demand and recurring home-cleaning services. Founded in Berlin and operating across 200+ cities in Germany and other European markets, the platform lets customers compare cleaner profiles and ratings, book and reschedule appointments, and pay online, with liability insurance covering each booking. Helpling operates as a consumer-facing web and mobile app product (iOS and Android) plus separate provider and agency portals; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation. It was surfaced through the point-nine venture portfolio and added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile.

providers.name: Home From College
providers.description: Home From College (H\FC) is an AI-powered growth platform that connects college students with paid work from consumer brands. Students earn money and build professional experience through microGIGs (quick paid tasks such as app installs, surveys, product feedback, and social sharing with instant payment) and GIGs (larger, ongoing opportunities including content creation, brand-ambassador roles, product testing, and internships), while brands reach and activate Gen Z talent for marketing campaigns. Backed by GV, Home From College runs a two-sided marketplace across a student mobile app and a brand-facing web platform. No public developer program, API documentation, or SDKs were found during enrichment.

providers.name: Jobbatical
providers.description: Jobbatical is a global mobility and immigration platform that helps companies manage international employee relocations, work visas, residence permits, and cross-border compliance across 45+ countries. It combines AI-powered case automation with expert immigration support to streamline eligibility assessments, visa and permit applications, renewal tracking, and settlement services for HR and mobility teams. The product centralizes case management, document processing, visa form automation, real-time status tracking, and renewal alerts, and offers pay-as-you-go or pre-purchased credit (FlexyPocket) pricing. Backed by Union Square Ventures.

providers.name: Simbel
providers.description: Simbel is a Paris-based HR technology company (founded 2021, backed by Speedinvest) offering a smart, unified training management suite that combines a Training Management System (TMS) and a Learning Management System (LMS) in one platform. It helps HR and L&D teams automate the full training lifecycle, from need assessment and request approvals through session organization, e-learning delivery, real-time reporting, and legal compliance (BPF, Qualiopi, BDES). Simbel connects to major HRIS and learning tools such as Workday, SAP SuccessFactors, ADP, Lucca, Payfit, BambooHR, 360Learning, and Docebo through pre-built integrations. As of this enrichment pass Simbel publishes no public developer API, API documentation, or developer portal; integrations are delivered as managed connectors rather than a self-serve public API.

providers.name: Visibly
providers.description: Visibly is a UK-based workforce compliance management platform that helps enterprises with large, distributed and subcontracted workforces automate their HSEQ (health, safety, environment and quality) obligations. It centralizes worker onboarding, competency and certification tracking, real-time compliance monitoring and alerts, audit and project reporting, and safety broadcast communications, with integrations into existing HR, ERP, LMS and SharePoint systems and mobile-first workflows for field workers. It is used across construction, manufacturing, FMCG, energy, public services, infrastructure and logistics by organizations including Network Rail, National Grid, EDF, Scottish Power, NHS and Danone. Backed by Creandum and Seedcamp.

providers.name: Wishup
providers.description: Wishup is a remote-work outsourcing platform that matches businesses with pre-vetted virtual assistants, bookkeepers, and automation specialists, typically onboarding a trained professional within 60 minutes. Its managed talent handles inbox and calendar management, CRM and social-media work, bookkeeping, project management, and AI-driven workflow automation across industries such as healthcare, e-commerce, real estate, startups, nonprofits, and legal services. Wishup runs a client-facing Employee Management App for task tracking and real-time feedback, but publishes no public developer API or developer portal.

providers.name: Happy5
providers.description: Happy5 is a Jakarta-based employee performance management platform, operated by Happy5 For The World Pte. Ltd. and founded in 2013, that unifies goal and OKR management, project tracking, and 360-degree performance reviews in one tool for HR teams. It automatically surfaces the goals hit, projects delivered, and milestones completed inside every performance review, and integrates with tools teams already use such as Jira, Asana, Slack, and Google Sheets. Its customers span major Indonesian banks, startups, and SMEs. Happy5 is a closed SaaS product and does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI definition, or client SDKs; this profile captures its verified public identity and web properties as a lead.

providers.name: Lara AI
providers.description: Lara AI is an AI agent for People and HR teams, built by SIGMA PEOPLE S.R.L. in Argentina and sold across Latin America. Lara talks to every employee in the messaging tools they already use — WhatsApp, Slack, Microsoft Teams and Google Chat — and covers five modules: Employee Experience (continuous listening, custom surveys and people analytics), Helpdesk (an AI help desk the company says automates over 80% of employee FAQs and requests), Onboarding (end-to-end automated flows for new hires), Comunicaciones (personalised, scheduled and segmented employee communications) and People Analytics (dashboards and reports built from people data). It integrates with HR platforms including SAP, BambooHR, Oracle, Buk, Humand, Mandu and Rex+, and targets retail, consumer goods, technology, consulting, banking and finance, education and manufacturing. Lara AI publishes a marketing site, a Spanish help centre and a real llms.txt, but no public API program — there is no developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI definition or SDK.

providers.name: Brown & Brown
providers.description: Brown & Brown, Inc. (NYSE: BRO) is a Daytona Beach, Florida headquartered insurance brokerage and risk-management intermediary founded in 1939, and one of the largest independent brokers in the United States. Following the 2025 acquisition of Accession Risk Management Group (Risk Strategies and One80 Intermediaries), it reports through two segments: Retail — property and casualty insurance, employee benefits, private client, captive solutions and financial/wealth services — and Specialty Distribution — programs, wholesale brokerage and MGA/binding-authority businesses including Arrowhead. As a distributor rather than a carrier, Brown & Brown places risk with insurers instead of underwriting it, and its US home market has no federal insurance regulator and no open-insurance mandate. Its API posture reflects that honestly: Brown & Brown publishes no public developer portal and no self-serve API. developer.bbrown.com, developers.bbrown.com, docs.bbrown.com and api.bbrown.com do not resolve, and every /developers, /api, /partners and /integrations path returns 404. Every discoverable application subdomain is a login wall — agent, client and vendor portals behind Microsoft Entra ID SSO or third-party sign-in. The only real programmatic surface is partner-gated: the Arrowhead Programs "Enterprise API" (EAPI), a quoting integration distributed through comparative raters and aggregators such as CoverHound, Tarmika, Semsee and DAIS, with no public documentation, base URL or specification. No ACORD, AL3, ACORD XML or NGDS reference is published on any Brown & Brown first-party property; carrier data exchange runs, as it does across US retail brokerage, through the agency management system layer — Brown & Brown is a publicly referenced Vertafore AMS360 agency — and IVANS agency download rather than through any API Brown & Brown itself exposes. In July 2026 the company announced an AI-first transformation with Anthropic, McKinsey and Accenture, deploying Claude across 23,000 teammates and Claude Code across its software engineering organization; that is internal adoption and has so far produced no external API, developer portal or agent-facing surface. The only machine-readable documents Brown & Brown publishes are two RSS feeds — the blog and investor news releases.

providers.name: Jobandtalent
providers.description: Jobandtalent is an AI-powered workforce marketplace that connects companies with reliable staff for temporary and permanent roles across logistics, warehousing, manufacturing, retail, and hospitality. Its platform combines a worker-facing mobile app for finding shifts and jobs with an employer-facing business platform for recruitment, shift planning, attendance management, and performance coaching. Founded in Spain and backed by Atomico, Jobandtalent operates across Europe, the US, and Latin America. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company's public developer, security, and compliance surface; the company publishes no public developer API at this time.

providers.name: Lantum
providers.description: Lantum (formerly Network Locum, founded 2012 in Shoreditch, London) is a United Kingdom healthcare workforce-management company whose Connected Scheduling platform helps NHS primary- and secondary-care organisations build digital staff banks, manage rotas and e-rostering, run automated timesheets and payments, and fill clinical shifts from a verified network of 30,000+ locum clinicians. It serves over 2,000 primary-care organisations, GP practices, PCNs, GP federations, and integrated care systems across the UK. Lantum is a practice-management and workforce platform rather than a clinical-data interoperability vendor, and it does NOT publish a public developer portal, a documented REST API, or an HL7 FHIR CapabilityStatement. Its product is delivered through a gated web and mobile application (lantum.com), onboarded via sales and demo request, with any system integrations (for example to GP clinical systems) handled through private partner arrangements rather than a self-serve public API.

providers.name: RippleHire
providers.description: RippleHire is an enterprise, AI-powered talent acquisition and Applicant Tracking System (ATS) that automates recruitment workflows end to end - demand creation, sourcing, employee referrals, candidate management, interviews, offers, and onboarding. Built on behavioral science, AI agents, and no-code configuration, it helps large organizations hire faster at scale across 50+ countries. Its RHConnect framework provides API-first and no-code integrations with HRMS, job boards, communication, and assessment tools. RippleHire is a portfolio company of 500 Global, added to the API Evangelist network and enriched by the pipeline.

providers.name: Upkid
providers.description: Upkid is a childcare staffing marketplace that connects early childhood programs such as daycares and preschools with qualified, pre-vetted substitute and full-time teachers. Programs post shifts and roles while educators find flexible teaching opportunities through the Upkid web and mobile apps, with an ATS-style Hiring Hub for full-time childcare hiring. Upkid operates across metro areas in Georgia, Utah, and Arizona and is a Techstars portfolio company. Upkid publishes no public API or developer portal; its web app is a client of a Firebase backend.

providers.name: Vida Health
providers.description: Vida Health is a San Francisco-based virtual care company founded in 2014 that combines an AI-powered mobile app with a national network of licensed clinicians, coaches and therapists to prevent, manage and reverse chronic cardiometabolic and behavioral health conditions including obesity, diabetes, hypertension, depression and anxiety. Vida sells a turnkey enterprise programme to employers and health plans, layering GLP-1 prescribing and clinical oversight on top of behavioral coaching, and its platform ingests real-time readings from more than 100 connected devices and consumer health apps to feed outcome reporting back to its enterprise buyers. Vida publishes no public developer portal or API documentation: the API host api.vida.com is live but returns 401 on every path, and data/EHR integration for health plans and employers is arranged through enterprise sales rather than self-service onboarding.

providers.name: WellTheory
providers.description: WellTheory is a virtual autoimmune care platform that provides whole-person support for people living with autoimmune and inflammatory conditions, pairing members with a dedicated care team for nutrition, lifestyle, and clinical guidance across more than 100 conditions. The company sells to employers and health plans as a covered benefit as well as direct to consumers, and is backed by Accel and General Catalyst. WellTheory publishes no public developer API surface today; its api.welltheory.com backend and docs are private/internal.

providers.name: Kinside
providers.description: Kinside is a modern child care marketplace that connects families with licensed child care providers by surfacing real-time availability across thousands of providers, helping parents find care in minutes rather than months. Beyond the consumer marketplace, Kinside serves child care providers with enrollment and scheduling tools, employers with child care benefit programs, and government agencies seeking community child care supply-and-demand data. Backed by Initialized Capital and Techstars, the company operates alongside UrbanSitter in the family-care benefits space. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network from venture-portfolio discovery; Kinside does not publish a public developer portal or API at this time, so this entry captures its public web, security, and identity surface.

providers.name: GLORRI, INC.
providers.description: Glorri is a cloud-based applicant tracking system (ATS) and recruitment automation platform for talent acquisition teams. It spans the entire hiring process, from sourcing candidates across multiple channels and job boards, to automating recruiting workflows and candidate communication, AI-assisted applicant screening, and analytics on team performance and hiring efficiency, with GDPR-compliant data handling. Glorri markets plans (Pay as you go, Flex, Corporate, and Enterprise Plus) for companies of different sizes, with custom integrations and a branded career page available on higher tiers. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network; as of this enrichment pass Glorri publishes a web application and marketing site but no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API specification.

providers.name: Paycor
providers.description: Paycor is a cloud-based human capital management (HCM) platform that provides payroll, HR, benefits administration, talent management, time and attendance, and workforce analytics for small and mid-sized businesses. The platform serves HR and finance teams with a unified system of record for employees, pay, time, and benefits data. Paycor exposes a Public REST API authenticated via OAuth 2.0 with authorization at secure.paycor.com and resource endpoints at apis.paycor.com (production) and apis-sandbox.paycor.com (sandbox).

providers.name: The Mom Project
providers.description: The Mom Project is a talent marketplace that connects skilled professionals (with a focus on mothers and caregivers) to remote, hybrid, and onsite roles at family-friendly employers. The platform pairs a community of hundreds of thousands of vetted candidates with thousands of companies through job matching, curated talent search, and managed hiring services such as pay-per-hire and access plans. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Initialized Capital and profiled in the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass, The Mom Project operates a consumer/employer web product and consumes third-party APIs (for example a Docusign eSignature integration for hiring workflows) but does not publish a public developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI, or other machine-readable API surface of its own.

providers.name: Billables Ai
providers.description: Billables AI is a San Francisco based legal technology company that builds AI-powered automatic time tracking software for lawyers, consultants, and professional services firms. Its platform passively captures billable activity as people work across the tools they already use — Microsoft 365, Outlook, Teams, Zoom, Adobe, and the Chrome and Edge browsers — then uses AI to draft time entries, assign the correct client and matter, and write narrative descriptions, learning and adapting to each user over time. Privacy is user-controlled, with only the individual able to view or edit their own time records before they are submitted. The company is venture-backed (Series A) and was surfaced through the Wing Venture Capital portfolio.

providers.name: Keep Financial
providers.description: Keep Financial Technologies, Inc. is a compensation technology company that provides a vesting cash bonus platform. Employers deliver upfront cash to employees that is earned (vests) over a customizable time period with a legally enforceable right to repayment, automating signing bonuses, retention bonuses, annual and performance bonuses, spot bonuses, tuition reimbursement, M&A retention packages, and severance. The platform serves compensation, HR, finance, legal, and executive leaders across healthcare, construction, logistics, technology, retail, hospitality, manufacturing, and other industries. Keep Financial was added to the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio company; it operates a SaaS web application and does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Twill
providers.description: Twill is a referral-based recruiting platform with the tagline "talent recommended talent." It makes hiring easier and faster by having a network of more than 50,000 vetted, experienced professionals across engineering, product, sales, and growth recommend their peers and friends for open roles, producing warm introductions to passive candidates instead of recruiter cold outreach. Twill advertises an average 22-day time to hire, a 90-day retention guarantee on placements, flat-fee pricing, and intelligent matching built in partnership with MIT's Generative AI Lab. The company is backed by Bloomberg Beta and does not currently publish a public developer API or API documentation; api.withtwill.com serves its private platform backend.

providers.name: doinstruct
providers.description: doinstruct is an AI-powered frontline training and compliance platform for deskless and shift-based workforces. Founded in Osnabrück, Germany in 2021 and now headquartered in Brooklyn, New York with an office in Berlin, it turns internal SOPs, documents, and expert knowledge into mobile-first courses delivered in 35+ languages. Its Genius AI authoring tool, a 400+ lesson training library, a manager dashboard for assigning and documenting training, and a mobile learner experience serve 400+ frontline teams across food & beverage, logistics, manufacturing, construction, and general compliance, with audit-ready reporting for standards such as HACCP, GFSI, and ISO 27001. Backed by Creandum and HV Capital.

providers.name: Heartland Payment Systems
providers.description: Heartland Payment Systems is a payment processing company offering payroll, customer engagement, point-of-sale, and other business solutions to merchants across the United States. Heartland is now a brand of Global Payments, and developer resources for Heartland integrations are published through the Global Payments developer portal. The platform supports online and in-person payments, bill pay, IoT/connected device payments, gift and loyalty, payroll, and PCI-validated point-to-point encryption.

providers.name: Hrmony
providers.description: Hrmony is a Berlin-based employee-benefits platform that lets German employers offer modern, tax-advantaged perks to their staff — meal allowances (Essenszuschuss), the 50 euro monthly non-cash benefit (Sachbezug) and benefit card, mobility and public-transit budgets, health and recreation benefits, internet-cost subsidies and digital gifts — all managed through an admin portal and employee app with built-in payroll and tax compliance. Its Hrmony Embedded product exposes this benefits infrastructure as a white-label RESTful API so software platforms and SaaS providers can integrate multiple benefit modules without building the tax-compliance, operations or regulatory layer in-house. Hrmony is backed by Techstars. This API Evangelist profile was enriched from the company's public web surface; no public developer documentation or OpenAPI is currently published (Embedded onboarding is partner-gated).

providers.name: LaborUp
providers.description: LaborUp is an AI-powered recruiting platform for American manufacturing, connecting skilled industrial workers — machinists, CNC programmers, welders, and maintenance technicians — with manufacturing employers. The platform combines voice-first AI screening, skills verification, and constraint-aware matching with dedicated recruiter support, and claims 5-10x faster hiring, more than 50% lower cost than traditional staffing agencies, 3x better post-hire retention, and a proprietary network of 25,000+ vetted workers. Founded by Simba Jonga, LaborUp raised $7.74M ($1.935M pre-seed plus a $5.8M seed announced in August 2025) led by NVP with Torch Capital, Threshold, Heartland VC, Daybreak, Westbound, Marketplace Capital, and Market Square Ventures. Early traction is concentrated in the Knoxville, Tennessee manufacturing corridor and in aerospace, shipbuilding, and critical infrastructure. As of July 2026 LaborUp publishes no public API, developer portal, or specification; the product is delivered as a hosted web and mobile application.

providers.name: Liftoff
providers.description: Liftoff (onliftoff.com, formerly liftoff.xyz) is a B2B network-based hiring and networking platform for startup leaders and hiring managers. Rather than cold applications or job-board sourcing, companies create a job search, attach a self-set "Match Incentive" referral bonus, and share the search link with their own network or with Liftoff's curated "Top Connectors" — senior leaders who refer pre-vetted candidates from their professional circles. Candidates surface through 2nd- and 3rd-degree trusted connections, and companies pay on a success-only basis, with fees due after a new hire completes 90 days. Liftoff targets seed-to-Series-B technology companies, primarily in the New York City and San Francisco ecosystems, and positions itself between LinkedIn recruiting and traditional retained search. Backed by Forerunner Ventures. Liftoff publishes no public API, SDK, or developer portal; it does publish an llms.txt for AI agent grounding. Not to be confused with Liftoff Mobile (liftoff.io, ad tech) or useLiftoff (useliftoff.com, job-seeker interview practice).

providers.name: Nova Benefits
providers.description: Nova Benefits is an India-based employee health and benefits platform that provides group health insurance, super top-up plans, and COVID-19 cover alongside wellness services such as telehealth consultations, mental-wellness support, fitness programs, maternity benefits, and annual health, dental and vision checkups. It gives HR teams an employer dashboard for administering benefits and managing claims, and gives employees web and mobile (iOS/Android) apps to view coverage, book consultations, and file and track claims. The company reports serving 500+ companies covering 200,000+ employees, is ISO 27001:2022 certified and SOC 2 Type II compliant, and operates as an IRDAI-regulated insurance broker. Nova Benefits publishes no public API or developer platform.

providers.name: Voya Financial
providers.description: Voya Financial (NYSE: VOYA) is a leading health, wealth, and investment company serving approximately 14.7 million individual, workplace, and institutional clients. Voya specializes in retirement plans, group employee benefits, health savings accounts (HSAs), and investment management. Their myVoyage platform integrates financial wellness tools to help participants plan, invest, and protect their financial futures. Voya does not offer a public developer API but provides account connectivity through open banking aggregators such as Plaid.

providers.name: Carrot Fertility
providers.description: Carrot Fertility is a global fertility and family-building benefits platform for employers and health plans, providing members with comprehensive reproductive and family-forming support across more than 195 countries. Carrot covers fertility care and preservation (egg, sperm, and embryo freezing), IVF and other assisted reproduction, surrogacy, adoption, pregnancy and postpartum support, low- and no-cost fertility options, gender-affirming care, and menopause and midlife care. Delivered as a B2B employee benefit with member and provider portals, Carrot pairs concierge care navigation with a network of clinics and experts. The company is HIPAA-compliant and maintains SOC 2 Type II, ISO/IEC 27001, PCI DSS, and HITRUST attestations. This API Evangelist profile tracks Carrot as a healthcare provider surfaced from the Uncork Capital portfolio; Carrot does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal.

providers.name: Clair
providers.description: Clair Inc is a New York-based financial technology company that provides free, compliant On-Demand Pay (earned wage access) as an embedded service inside the payroll, time-and-attendance and workforce-management platforms employees already use. Rather than selling a consumer app, Clair partners with platforms — Gusto Embedded Payroll, Check, 7shifts and others — and connects to them over a partner REST API that transmits employee, employment and attendance data, which Clair's underwriting engine uses to originate 0% APR earned wage advances through its FDIC-insured partner bank, Pathward N.A. Partners embed a Clair-hosted user experience (a WebView component, distributed for iOS as Swift packages) so employees can take an advance, review history and handle loan servicing without a separate login. Clair has raised roughly $218M in total capital, including a $23.2M Series B in May 2025.

providers.name: dopay
providers.description: dopay is a digital payroll platform operating in Egypt that lets employers register employees and disburse salaries in minutes through a single system, including permanent, temporary, and seasonal workers across construction, agriculture, hospitality, retail, healthcare, education, and manufacturing. Supervised by a bank and regulated by the Central Bank of Egypt, dopay digitizes cash-based wage payments and pairs core Salary Disbursement with an Early Pay earned-wage-access product that lets employees withdraw part of their salary before payday. Originally a Techstars-backed fintech focused on banking the unbanked, dopay is added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it publishes a business web app and login but no public developer API, portal, or documentation at this time.

providers.name: Fastwork
providers.description: Fastwork is Thailand's leading freelance and services marketplace, connecting businesses and individuals with roughly 200,000 vetted service providers across about 300 categories — including design and graphics, web and app development, AI development and automation, marketing and advertising, writing and translation, photography and video, and lifestyle services. An escrow-based "Fastwork Guarantee" holds payment until work is delivered, protecting both buyers and freelancers. The platform serves individuals, SMEs, and enterprises with a dedicated business portal, and is expanding from Thailand into Indonesia and Vietnam. Fastwork is backed by 500 Global and Partech. No public developer API is currently published; this profile captures the company's public web surface and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Fiverr
providers.description: Fiverr is a global online marketplace for freelance digital services, founded in 2010 and headquartered in Tel Aviv, Israel, and publicly traded on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE: FVRR). The platform connects businesses and individuals with freelancers offering "gigs" across hundreds of categories including graphic design, writing and translation, programming and tech, video and animation, digital marketing, music and audio, and AI services. Fiverr also operates Fiverr Pro and Fiverr Enterprise for vetted talent and managed teams, Fiverr Workspace for freelancer business tooling, and an affiliate partnership program. Fiverr does not currently publish a public developer API portal or OpenAPI-described API; its programmatic surfaces are limited to the consumer marketplace and partner/affiliate integrations. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and Bessemer Venture Partners and enriched with the public identity, security, and discovery signals available.

providers.name: Terminal
providers.description: Terminal (terminal.io) is a talent platform for hiring vetted remote and nearshore software engineers for full-time, contract, and contract-to-hire roles. It combines AI-fluency assessment and technical vetting (accepting roughly the top 7% of applicants) with Employer of Record (EOR) services that handle HR, payroll, and benefits across 180+ countries, sourcing engineers from Latin America, Canada, and Europe. Terminal is a B2B staffing and hiring platform rather than an API provider — it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal. Backed by 8VC and Lightspeed Venture Partners; added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile.

providers.name: Torch
providers.description: Torch (Redfish Labs, Inc. dba Torch Leadership Labs) is a leadership development and executive coaching platform that pairs expert human coaches with AI to help mid-market and enterprise organizations grow leaders and navigate change. Its offerings include Change Coaching (leaders-turned-coaches trained in Torch's change approach), the Spark AI coaching agent (always-on AI guidance for practicing conversations and turning insight into progress), and Organizational Intelligence (real-time visibility into change patterns and people dynamics). Torch focuses on AI transformation, organizational restructuring, organizational resilience, and leadership growth, and counts Airbnb, Reddit, Tripadvisor, FICO, and Twitch among its customers. Torch is a SaaS product with SSO (SAML), Zoom, and Slack integrations but publishes no public developer API; this profile captures its public identity and security posture.

providers.name: Arc
providers.description: Arc (arc.dev, formerly CodementorX, and sister to the Codementor mentorship marketplace) is a remote talent marketplace that connects companies with vetted freelance and full-time software developers, designers, marketers, and product managers across 190 countries. Arc screens applicants down to roughly the top 2%, and partners with Deel and Remote for cross-border payroll and compliance. Arc operates as a hiring platform and does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or webhook surface.

providers.name: AllCare
providers.description: AllCare is a Philippines-based digital employee-benefits and healthcare membership platform for freelancers and small-to-medium enterprises. It aggregates worker benefits that individuals and small teams would otherwise struggle to access, bundling HMO coverage, group life insurance, 24/7 teleconsultation, dental and optical care, mental-health counseling, annual physical exams, and productivity perks into flat-rate membership packages. Its SME Benefits Package is sold on an annual per-employee basis (minimum five employees) and is managed through a web dashboard for enrollment, member management, and benefit utilization. AllCare is a portfolio company of 500 Global and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a healthcare/insurtech company profile.

providers.name: Centivo
providers.description: Centivo is a primary-care-centered health plan administrator for self-funded employers, founded in 2017 and headquartered in New York City. Sold through benefits brokers and consultants, it serves mid-market employers (roughly 50 or more employees) and covers about 77,000 members across 160 businesses. Members get $0 primary care to encourage early intervention, and employers typically save 15-30% versus traditional fully-insured plans through a primary-care-first model, the cost advantages of self-funding, and directly negotiated health-system partnerships. Centivo operates member, employer, provider, and referral portals plus iOS/Android member apps; it does not publish a public developer API. Backed by Bain Capital Ventures and JPMorgan Chase's Morgan Health.

providers.name: Newfront Insurance
providers.description: Newfront is a technology-native insurance brokerage ("a brokerage for the 21st century") serving startups through Fortune 500 enterprises, and now part of WTW. It places business insurance (property, casualty, cyber, executive risk, workers' compensation, surety, aviation, M&A and global programs) alongside Total Rewards services (employee benefits, compensation, retirement/401(k), HR, payroll and benefits compliance), pairing brokerage expertise with in-house software such as the Navigator benefits platform, RiskPulse analytics, and contract/coverage-gap review tools. Newfront reports roughly 20% of U.S. unicorns as clients and $3.1B in annual premiums placed. The company exposes no public developer API, documentation, developer portal, SDKs, or webhooks; client and employee interaction happens through the authenticated app.newfront.com application. This profile was surfaced as a VC portfolio company and enriched with company identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Simplyinsured
providers.description: SimplyInsured is a small-business health insurance brokerage and online enrollment platform. It aggregates medical, dental, and vision plans from major carriers, provides unbiased plan recommendations, and lets small employers compare, quote, and enroll their teams entirely online at no cost to the business. Founded in 2012 and backed by Y Combinator, SimplyInsured is frequently embedded as the health-insurance offering inside partner payroll and HR platforms. As of this enrichment pass the company exposes a consumer-facing web application and a support/help surface but publishes no public developer API, SDKs, OpenAPI, or developer portal.

providers.name: TaTiO
providers.description: TaTiO is a recruitment and candidate-assessment platform that replaces traditional resume-based screening with immersive, AI-driven virtual job simulations. Candidates perform real job tasks - a forklift pre-shift check, a customer service call - so employers see how they actually work rather than how they describe themselves, producing a prediction score, a skills snapshot, and a report drawn from roughly 150 data points per candidate. The platform aims to increase application and engagement rates, reduce hiring mismatches, and integrate with existing hiring tools (ATS) so candidate status syncs automatically. TaTiO is a Techstars-backed company; its public website runs on Wix and exposes a hosted Wix Site MCP endpoint for agentic AI access.

providers.name: Swept
providers.description: Swept (sweptworks.com) is workforce management software for commercial cleaning and janitorial businesses - scheduling, GPS-verified time tracking and payroll reporting, mobile crew messaging, quality inspections, supply requests, client portals, and one-time work order management. As of this catalog entry, Swept does NOT publish a documented, self-serve public or partner developer API. There is no developer portal, API reference, API key or OAuth signup, published OpenAPI/Swagger specification, or webhook documentation on sweptworks.com or in the Swept Support Center knowledge base. The only documented outbound data path is a one-way, manually-activated QuickBooks Online payroll sync set up per account by a Swept Customer Success Manager - not a self-serve developer integration. Swept's public GitHub organization contains only take-home coding-challenge repositories used for hiring, not a first-party API client, SDK, or spec. This entry is therefore an honest stub documenting the provider and its access model; no API definitions are asserted because none are publicly documented.

providers.name: EAT Club
providers.description: EAT Club is a corporate meal-delivery platform founded in 2010 in Redwood City, California by Kevin Yang and Rodrigo Santibanez, built around the idea of a "virtual cafeteria" for offices with no on-site dining. Instead of tray-style catering, each employee picks an individually packaged meal from a rotating daily menu produced by EAT Club's own kitchens and restaurant partners, and every order for a building arrives in one synchronized delivery. The company markets the program as an employee lunch benefit and reports 21 million meals delivered to roughly 1,145 companies across nine cities. Compass Group USA acquired EAT Club in October 2020 and folded its ordering, production and delivery technology into Compass Digital Labs, where it now underpins workplace, education and healthcare dining accounts across the US and Canada. The consumer-facing product is a React ordering app served from www.eatclub.com; EAT Club publishes no developer program, no API reference, no SDK and no machine-readable contract of any kind.

providers.name: PitchMe
providers.description: PitchMe is a recruitment data intelligence platform that enriches, verifies, and deduplicates candidate records to turn an existing ATS or CRM database into an activated talent pool. It cleans and appends verified contact details, employment history, and skills data, then surfaces career-intelligence signals that power AI-driven sourcing and outreach. PitchMe connects to applicant tracking systems such as Bullhorn, Greenhouse, Salesforce, Lever, JobDiva, Vincere, Avionte, Jobvite, and Ashby via native and certified integrations, plus a custom API for connecting any ATS or recruitment platform. Backed by Techstars.

providers.name: Robert Half International
providers.description: Robert Half International is the world's first and largest specialized staffing and talent solutions firm. Founded in 1948, it provides contract, temporary, and permanent placement solutions across finance and accounting, technology, marketing, legal, and administrative fields. The company is the parent of Protiviti, a global consulting firm. Robert Half does not publicly expose a developer API; integration is available through partner programs and ATS ecosystem connectors. Listed in the Fortune 500.

providers.name: BrightPlan
providers.description: BrightPlan is a San Jose, California based financial wellness company that sells a Total Financial Wellness platform to enterprise HR and benefits teams, combining a self-service digital financial planning application, an AI-powered financial wellness coach, and access to human CFP fiduciary advisors. BrightPlan LLC is an SEC-registered investment adviser, and the product is delivered to employees as an employer-sponsored benefit rather than as a self-serve consumer subscription. The employee experience runs at my.brightplan.com and web.brightplan.com with iOS and Android apps; employer value is framed around benefits engagement, retention, and measurable financial wellbeing. BrightPlan markets HRIS and benefits-system integration to employers but publishes no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: Calvis
providers.description: Calvis is a multi-agency security guard marketplace that connects businesses with vetted, state-licensed, background-checked security guards from multiple professional agencies across 40+ US cities. Founded in 2023 and headquartered in Miami, Florida, the platform pairs on-demand booking with AI-powered deployment matching, real-time GPS tracking and geofencing, live AI coaching delivered to guards through an earpiece, and automated incident reporting and site analytics. Businesses book unarmed, armed, event, retail, construction, corporate, residential, hospital, cannabis, and school security through the web platform and iOS/Android apps, while security professionals join the network to find work. Calvis is backed by Version One Ventures.

providers.name: Clockster
providers.description: Clockster is a frontline staff-management super-app for food & beverage and retail businesses, consolidating attendance and time tracking, shift scheduling, automated payroll, earned wage access, business communication, tasks and checklists into a single mobile-first platform. Founded in 2018 and headquartered in Singapore with offices across Kazakhstan and Indonesia, Clockster serves more than 1,300 SMEs across Central and Southeast Asia — including brands such as KFC, Hardee's and Costa Coffee — and is backed by 500 Global, I2BF Global Ventures and Quest Ventures. It is delivered as iOS, Android and Huawei mobile apps plus a web console and currently exposes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Epsor
providers.description: Epsor is a French fintech, founded in 2017, that manages employee savings and retirement plans (épargne salariale et retraite) for companies and helps them turn that benefit into an HR lever. A certified B Corp and mission-driven company, Epsor ranks among the top 10 employee-savings and retirement providers in France and serves more than 2,500 corporate clients. It targets HR, Compensation & Benefits, and Finance teams at mid-size and large French firms, combining a pedagogical, personalized saver experience, an open-architecture fund range (40+ funds from 15+ asset managers, with a strong ESG/SRI focus), and year-round support to run and promote the plan. Epsor is neither an asset manager nor a bank: it is the single point of contact for companies and their employees, and delegates account-keeping to Société Générale Securities Services (SGSS). Products span PEE, PER Collectif (PERECO), PER Obligatoire, intéressement, participation, abondement, and employee share ownership. Epsor exposes no public developer API; this profile captures its public identity and security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Fertifa
providers.description: Fertifa is Europe's reproductive healthcare benefits provider for employers, giving companies a way to offer fertility, family-forming, women's health, maternity, menopause, men's reproductive health, and neurodiversity support to their employees. The platform pairs an in-house clinical team with education and training, diagnostics and testing, prescriptions and medication delivery, and financing/reimbursement, delivered to staff through a mobile app and to HR teams through enterprise and SME plans. Fertifa is London-based, backed by Speedinvest, and works with employers including Lululemon, Meta, Bain Capital, and Virgin. No public developer API or OpenAPI surface is currently published; this profile captures the company's public web, legal, and support properties.

providers.name: Incluyeme
providers.description: Incluyeme.com is a Latin American social enterprise, founded in 2013 by Gabriel Marcolongo, working toward the social and labor inclusion of people with disabilities. Its online platform connects candidates with disabilities to inclusive employers, offering job listings, virtual training courses, scholarships, and mentorship for individuals, alongside inclusive-hiring consulting, talent sourcing, staff training, and physical/web accessibility evaluation for companies. Operating across roughly a dozen countries in Latin America (Argentina, Chile, Peru, Colombia, Mexico, Uruguay, Paraguay and more), it has registered hundreds of thousands of people with disabilities and placed thousands into roles with 100+ corporate clients. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and profiled in the API Evangelist network; it publishes no public developer API.

providers.name: Paro
providers.description: Paro is an AI-powered professional services marketplace that connects businesses and accounting firms with vetted, on-demand finance and accounting experts. Founded in 2015 and headquartered in Chicago, Paro uses proprietary AI matching to pair clients with the top 2% of finance professionals across 60+ industries and 250+ skill sets — spanning bookkeeping, fractional CFO and controller services, financial planning and analysis, tax and compliance, and full-time recruiting. For accounting firms it provides staff augmentation, busy-season support, and service-expansion consulting. Paro operates a talent platform (app.paro.io) but does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures its identity, content, and public web surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: RippleMatch
providers.description: RippleMatch is an AI-powered early-career recruiting platform that matches college students and recent graduates with internships and entry-level jobs based on their background, skills, and career goals rather than mass applications. For employers it offers "Campus OS", an all-in-one recruiting operating system for sourcing, skills validation, and campus event management, and it transfers matched candidates into most major applicant tracking systems (Greenhouse, Workday, Lever, SmartRecruiters, BambooHR). RippleMatch was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bullpen Capital and profiled in the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or webhook/event surface; its integrations are one-way ATS data transfers rather than an openly documented API.

providers.name: Saffron
providers.description: Saffron (trysaffron.ai) is a Y Combinator (Spring 2026) startup building an AI-native technical assessment platform for engineering hiring. Candidates build real features on a company's actual codebase using AI coding tools such as Claude Code inside a sandboxed environment, while Saffron captures every keystroke and AI interaction to score submissions against custom rubrics. It provides line-by-line attribution distinguishing human-written, AI-generated, and AI-modified code, and replaces traditional phone screens, take-homes, and on-site interview loops with a single AI-integrated assessment.

providers.name: Topia
providers.description: Topia is a global mobility platform for distributed workforces, used by HR, Finance and Legal teams at mid-market and enterprise companies to manage international assignments, relocations, business travel, remote work and cross-border compliance across 190+ countries in a single system. Founded in 2010 and headquartered in the United States, with additional offices in the United Kingdom, Ireland and Estonia, Topia spans global talent mobility, a tax and compliance engine, cost estimation and tracking, global workforce planning, cost and immigration risk management, and business travel. In April 2026 Topia launched Horizon, an agentic AI workspace for mobility teams that the company describes as built natively into MCP (Model Context Protocol) environments. Topia integrates with HRIS, payroll, travel and expense systems including Workday (a Workday Approved Integration), SAP, ADP, Oracle, Ceridian, SAP Concur and BCD Travel. Topia publishes an llms.txt at its marketing host, but no public developer portal, API reference or machine-readable specification; the support center sits behind a customer login.

providers.name: XP Health
providers.description: XP Health is an AI-powered vision benefits platform that modernizes employer vision programs with full-replacement and dual-option plans designed to reduce employee out-of-pocket eyewear costs. The platform serves more than 6,300 organizations, offering in-app prescription renewals, virtual try-on across 5,000+ eyewear styles, and a provider network reaching 90% of the U.S. population, with members saving an average of 69% on eyewear claims. Backed by QED Investors. XP Health does not currently publish a public developer portal or API.

providers.name: Andela
providers.description: Andela is a global talent platform and AI services provider founded in 2014 by Jeremy Johnson, connecting enterprises with vetted, remote technologists and AI engineers across 135+ countries. It grew into a unicorn (valued at $1.5B in 2021) serving 650+ clients, with a network of 200,000+ trained technologists. Its services span hiring AI engineers for application building, systems integration, and platform engineering; building enterprise AI solutions from data readiness to production deployment; and upskilling teams through AI curricula developed with partners such as NVIDIA and Google. Andela operates a fully remote model and is backed by GV, SoftBank Vision Fund, and Susa Ventures. It publishes no public developer API.

providers.name: BallerTV
providers.description: BallerTV (Baller, Inc.) is a Pasadena, California sports media company that live streams and provides on-demand replays and highlights of youth and amateur sports, including basketball, volleyball, soccer, lacrosse, softball, and football, from thousands of tournaments and showcases nationwide. Subscribers range from families following athletes to NCAA and professional scouts using the footage for recruiting and scouting. The platform includes a Game Finder for locating events, purchasable athlete highlight reels, and BTVision, an AI-powered ball-tracking streaming technology that improves the basketball viewing experience. BallerTV is a consumer streaming product delivered through its website and iOS/Android apps; it does not publish a public developer API or SDK program. This profile was surfaced as an index-ventures portfolio company and enriched from public web sources.

providers.name: Foodsmart
providers.description: Foodsmart is a telenutrition company that pairs the nation's largest network of registered dietitians with a digital food-benefits platform, delivering personalized nutrition care via telehealth to more than three million members. The company partners with health plans and employers to reach Medicaid, Medicare, and commercial members, combining one-on-one dietitian counseling with meal planning, grocery ordering, and SNAP benefits enrollment. Foodsmart's "Foodscription" model connects clinical nutrition guidance to affordable, healthy food access to improve outcomes and lower the cost of diet-related chronic disease. This profile was surfaced as a Mayfield portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Foodsmart exposes no public developer API, SDKs, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: M7 Health
providers.description: M7 Health is an AI-powered workforce operations platform for healthcare, focused on nurse scheduling and labor optimization. The platform forecasts staffing demand, auto-balances schedules, fills open shifts, and deploys staff to close coverage gaps while reducing premium labor spend, administrative burden, and nurse turnover across hospitals and health systems. Surfaced as a portfolio company of threshold-ventures and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; no public developer or API surface was found — the product is delivered as an enterprise SaaS engaged via a sales demo.

providers.name: Medely
providers.description: Medely is a healthcare workforce orchestration platform and staffing marketplace that connects healthcare facilities with a network of qualified nurses and allied health professionals. What began as a marketplace to match facilities with per-diem talent has grown into a full workforce management platform, helping hospitals, surgery centers, skilled nursing facilities, and other providers fill open and per-diem shifts, support their core clinical teams, and maintain high-quality patient care. Medely offers credentialing, scheduling, and flexible workforce management tools, and holds the Joint Commission's Gold Seal of Approval for its staffing services. The company is backed by General Catalyst and Wing Venture Capital. Medely does not currently operate a public developer program or documented API; its GraphQL backend at api.medely.com powers the first-party web and mobile applications only.

providers.name: Radish Health
providers.description: Radish Health is a healthcare company that provides employers with a modern employee health benefit, pairing each member with a dedicated care team and physicians who handle medical issues directly or coordinate specialist referrals. The service emphasizes direct-access primary care over phone, video, and in-person visits, with rapid response times and appointment coordination aimed at reducing employer healthcare costs while improving the patient experience. Radish Health is delivered through patient-facing web and mobile apps (iOS and Android) and an employer benefits program; it is a Techstars portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass, Radish Health publishes no public API, developer portal, or technical documentation — this profile captures its identity, legal/support surfaces, and domain security posture only.

providers.name: Refyne
providers.description: Refyne is an Indian financial wellness platform and the country's first earned wage access (EWA) provider, letting employees draw a portion of their already-earned salary before payday at 0% interest through their employer's payroll. Founded in 2020 and backed by QED Investors, Refyne serves 500+ organizations across 23 industries and more than 8 million employees, and operates additional products including RuPay credit cards, the MoneyGuru financial-literacy service, and an employee privilege/discount club. The company operates under RBI compliance and holds ISO 27001 and SOC 2 certifications. Refyne is primarily a B2B2C mobile and payroll-integrated platform and does not publish a public developer portal or API at this time; this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: SafelyYou
providers.description: SafelyYou is an ambient-AI platform for senior living communities that reduces falls, reveals resident risk, and surfaces operational and staffing insights without requiring residents to wear devices. Its computer-vision system detects and reviews fall incidents, and the broader product suite spans Safety AI for fall detection, Staffing AI for labor allocation and care tracking, Wellness AI for resident well-being, the Halo next-generation eCall system, and Guardian hardware sensors. SafelyYou reports serving over 1,000 communities and 50,000 residents, with outcomes including roughly 45% fall reduction and longer length of stay. The company integrates with senior-living EHR and eCall systems (Yardi, ALIS, PointClickCare and others) and offers SSO, but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Zehitomo
providers.description: Zehitomo is a Tokyo-based online marketplace that matches consumers in Japan with local professionals across hundreds of service categories — including photographers, personal trainers, house cleaners, graphic and web designers, videographers, tax accountants, interpreters, construction and repair trades, and business consultants. Clients describe the job they need done and receive quotes and proposals from vetted local pros, while professionals pay to respond to matched leads. Founded in 2015 and backed by 500 Global, Zehitomo runs a consumer-facing web and mobile product; it does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: coachhub
providers.description: CoachHub is a global digital coaching platform (headquartered in Berlin) that lets enterprises deliver scalable, measurable one-to-one coaching to their entire workforce through web and mobile apps. Its network spans 3,500+ certified business coaches across 90+ countries with sessions in 80+ languages, matched to learners via AI, and it ships an AI coaching companion (AIMY). CoachHub serves 1,000+ enterprise clients and is backed by SoftBank Vision Fund 2, Sofina, HV Capital, Partech and Speedinvest. It offers an account-managed integration approach (SSO, automated provisioning and data sync) with HR/LMS systems such as Workday, SAP, Oracle, Ceridian and Microsoft Teams, but publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs or GitHub repositories. The platform is ISO 27001, ISO 27701, SOC 2 Type II, TISAX and PCI DSS Level 1 certified and GDPR/CCPA compliant.

providers.name: Electric Car Scheme
providers.description: The Electric Car Scheme is a UK B Corp providing electric vehicle salary sacrifice as an employee benefit. Employees lease any electric car of their choice with the monthly cost deducted from gross salary before Income Tax and National Insurance, saving 20-50% versus a personal lease, while employers save on Class 1A National Insurance. Packages are all-inclusive (lease, insurance, maintenance, servicing and breakdown) with Complete Protection covering employees who leave partway through a lease term. The company integrates with employer payroll systems via API or SFTP and offers Single Sign-On for employees, plus an included Charge Scheme for charging access.

providers.name: Grade
providers.description: Grade is the API for performance-based payroll, letting companies pay workers, creators, contractors, and AI agents based on results rather than hours worked. Companies push performance signals into Grade via webhooks or direct API calls (task completed, milestone hit, content published, views tracked, invoice processed), and Grade runs them against configurable payout rules — flat fees, tiered commissions, threshold bonuses, or blended structures — handling the math, de-duplication, and approval workflows automatically. Grade tracks every post across platforms, approves and distributes bulk payouts in one click, and handles compliance end to end: KYC verification, tax-form collection, DAC7 reporting, worker classification, and merchant-of-record services. Payouts reach 190+ countries via local bank transfers, PayPal, Wise, Payoneer, Revolut, Airtm, and USDT, with no separate creator account required. Grade (YC W26) is based in San Francisco and has paid out $10M+ to date.

providers.name: Spring Health
providers.description: Spring Health is a New York City-based digital mental health company that sells a comprehensive mental healthcare benefit to employers, health plans, brokers, channel partners, and healthcare providers. Its platform combines a clinically validated assessment, AI-driven matching, and a curated provider network to deliver therapy, medication management, coaching, an Employee Assistance Program (EAP), critical-incident response, work-life services, and self-guided digital exercises through a unified member experience branded Spring Life. For health plans and providers, Spring Health offers Springworks — its enterprise care-coordination and care-management offering — alongside a generative-AI member-facing assistant called Guide and clinician-facing AI tooling. Customers include General Mills, Hearst, and Moda Health, and the company publishes outcomes, research, and ROI evidence on long-term cost savings of mental health benefits. Spring Health operates as a B2B2C benefit: it does not expose a public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or documented HTTP API. Integrations with HRIS, SSO, eligibility files, and health-plan partners are delivered through enterprise implementation rather than a self-service API, and its GitHub organization (github.com/SpringHealth) has no public repositories.

providers.name: Headspace
providers.description: Headspace (formerly Headspace Health, the 2021 merger of Headspace and Ginger) is a mental health and wellbeing company best known for its consumer meditation, mindfulness, and sleep app, alongside an enterprise business that delivers coaching, therapy, and psychiatry to employers, health plans, and healthcare providers. The consumer app offers guided meditation, sleepcasts, focus music, and mindful movement, while Headspace for Organizations provides clinical mental healthcare and EAP-style benefits at scale. Headspace does not currently publish a public developer platform, API, or SDKs; integrations are handled through enterprise partnerships (for example health-plan and benefits-platform data exchanges), and its engineering work is visible through the headspacemeditation GitHub organization. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a Khosla Ventures portfolio lead and enriched with the public identity, security posture, and web properties that could be verified.

providers.name: Lumity
providers.description: Lumity is a digital employee benefits broker (part of Alera Group) that acts as an extension of HR teams, combining benefits-administration technology with dedicated benefits experts. Its platform centralizes plan management, eligibility, employee enrollment (web and mobile), renewal strategy and negotiation, year-round employee support, PEO migration, and reporting/analytics with cost forecasting. Lumity markets outcomes such as average cost savings through smarter plan selection and per-employee annual savings. It surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Threshold Ventures (fintech). Enrichment found no first-party public API, developer portal, or specifications: the employer login portal (er-portal.lumity.com) redirects to the third-party PlanYear platform, and legal pages are served under Alera Group.

providers.name: Accolade
providers.description: Accolade is a personalized healthcare and benefits navigation platform for employers and health plans. It pairs members with a care team of advocates, registered nurses, physicians, and mental-health specialists to help them understand their benefits, find in-network care, book appointments, and manage chronic and complex conditions. Accolade combines this human advocacy with virtual primary care, expert medical opinion, and mental-health services delivered through its member web and mobile apps. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network. Accolade is a member-facing benefits platform and does not publish a public API, developer portal, or developer documentation.

providers.name: Leland
providers.description: Leland is a marketplace for ambitious people to access the coaching, classes, and community they need to reach career and educational goals. It connects individuals with vetted 1-on-1 coaches across MBA and college admissions, management consulting, investment banking, private equity, product management, law, medicine, and executive and career development, and sells structured live programs, bootcamps, and test prep for the GMAT, GRE, LSAT, MCAT, SAT, and ACT. Leland+ is a subscription content library of video guides, essay and resume examples, templates, and expert-built AI tools. For organizations Leland offers AI-native talent training, agentic workflow deployment, recruiting, and outplacement, plus university and HR partnerships. Leland publishes no public API or developer portal as of 2026-07-19.

providers.name: Milu Health
providers.description: Milu Health is a health technology company that pairs a virtual care team with an AI engine to help employees and their families get higher-quality healthcare at a lower cost. Founded in 2023 by Sasha Gribov and Gautam Kumar, Milu integrates directly with electronic health record (EHR) data from tens of thousands of provider groups and health systems to proactively flag medication issues, care gaps, fairly priced and high-quality doctors, incorrect medical bills, and more affordable medications. The platform also ingests an employer's health plan and benefits so it can notify members when an existing benefit could help. Milu is offered through employers and benefits advisors as well as directly to individuals. The company raised a $4.8M seed round led by a16z Bio + Health in March 2024. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio company; Milu does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Mottu
providers.description: Mottu is the leading motorcycle-rental ecosystem in Latin America, founded in 2020 in Sao Paulo, Brazil by Rubens Zanelatto. It rents motorcycles to gig and delivery couriers who lack access to traditional credit, bundling insurance, maintenance, 24-hour support and financial services (Mottu Pay) so workers can earn income through food delivery, e-commerce and last-mile logistics. Mottu has verticalized the value chain, running its own assembly line, parts and service network, and fleet-management software, and offers white-labeled last-mile delivery (Mottu Entregas) to more than 1,000 retailers across 100+ cities in Brazil and Mexico. Backed by QED Investors, Mottu has raised over US$150M. It operates as a consumer and B2B mobility/fintech app and does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: The Helper Bees
providers.description: The Helper Bees is an Austin-based aging-in-place technology company that operates one connected platform linking benefits, in-home service providers, and support so older adults can safely age at home. Its products include Care Concierge human guidance, an Aging-in-Place Marketplace for OTC products and nonmedical services (home care, safety modifications, meals, transportation), the Helpful benefits card, digital invoicing and claims processing for home and facility care, and digital nurse eligibility assessments for long-term care insurance. The company runs one of the nation's largest networks of vetted in-home care agencies and sells to Long-Term Care Insurance, Medicare Advantage, and Medicaid plan administrators. It was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. The Helper Bees publishes member and provider applications (the api.thehelperbees.com app host, the myhomealign.com provider portal, and mobile apps) but does not currently expose a public developer program, OpenAPI specification, or SDKs.

providers.name: Knoetic
providers.description: Knoetic is an HR technology company that operates CPOHQ, a platform built for Chief People Officers and senior people-function executives. The product combines three surfaces: a private, invite-only community of 3,000+ Chief People Officers (one member per company) who exchange confidential playbooks and benchmarks; an AI "Chief of Staff" that delivers personalized morning briefings and monitors market and talent trends; and a suite of workflow-specific AI agents for people analytics, performance insight, and peer benchmarking across the people function. The company was founded as Knoetic around a people-analytics product and has since consolidated its public brand on CPOHQ — knoetic.com now redirects to cpohq.com, while the customer application remains at app.knoetic.com. Knoetic has raised $50M+ from Accel, EQT Ventures, Menlo Ventures and angel investors. As of this enrichment pass Knoetic publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or API documentation; the platform is a closed B2B SaaS offering sold to enterprise people teams. It does publish a Vanta-hosted trust center and displays a SOC 2 Type II attestation.

providers.name: Lagou
providers.description: Lagou (拉勾招聘) is a Chinese online recruitment platform operated by Beijing Lagou Network Technology Co., Ltd., focused on hiring for the internet and technology sector. It matches software engineers, product managers, designers and other digital-economy professionals with employers across major Chinese cities, publishing verified job listings alongside a browseable directory of hiring companies. Around the core job board it runs Lagou Enterprise (easy.lagou.com) for employer-side recruiting, Lagou Campus (xiaoyuan.lagou.com) for graduate hiring, and Lagou Education (kaiwu.lagou.com) for professional-skills courses. Lagou was surfaced through the Qiming Venture Partners portfolio. It publishes no public API, developer portal or API documentation — open.lagou.com carries a "Lagou Open Platform" title but serves only a stub page — so this profile captures the company's public web and security surface rather than an API surface.

providers.name: Wisq
providers.description: Wisq is an AI platform for human resources that automates HR service management, HR operations, and employee relations. Its conversational AI HR agent, Harper, answers employee requests across chat, email, Slack, Teams, SMS, and mobile, while its proprietary HR Language Model (HRLM) provides HR-specific reasoning, aiming to resolve the majority of routine HR cases without a human in the loop. Founded by Jim Barnett and Chih-Po Wen (formerly of Glint), Wisq is backed by Norwest Venture Partners, Shasta Ventures, and True Ventures. Wisq operates a private, login-gated product and publishes no public developer API at this time.

providers.name: Chief Human Capital Officers Council
providers.description: The Chief Human Capital Officers (CHCO) Council is the principal interagency forum to advise and coordinate the activities of members on matters of modernization of human resources (HR) systems, improved quality of human resources information, and legislation affecting human resources operations and organizations across the U.S. federal government. Established under the Chief Human Capital Officers Act of 2002 (5 U.S.C. 1401-1402), the Council is chaired by the Director of the U.S. Office of Personnel Management (OPM) with the Deputy Director for Management at OMB serving as Vice Chair.
