providers.description: Job search app and website

providers.name: Brighter
providers.description: Brighter is a Santa Monica, California digital health technology company founded in 2010 by internet entrepreneur Jake Winebaum that built a consumer-driven dental benefits platform connecting dentists, patients, and dental insurers. Brighter licensed digital engagement solutions to insurance carriers, including online and mobile provider directories, patient reviews, and its proprietary Brighter Schedule online appointment scheduling feature, along with the Brighter PRO self-insured dental plan launched in 2014. Its platform powered member-engagement tools for major dental insurers including Cigna, Delta Dental, and Aetna. Backed by roughly $49M from General Catalyst, Mayfield, Benchmark, DAG Ventures, and Tenaya Capital, Brighter was acquired by Cigna in December 2017 and its technology folded into Cigna's digital health offerings. The brand persists as a Cigna dental provider experience.

providers.name: Gigmile
providers.description: Gigmile is an African mobility platform and gig-economy fintech that gives riders, drivers, and fleet operators a pathway to financial independence through affordable vehicle financing and operational support. It offers lease-to-own and flexible financing for motorcycles, tricycles, cars, and electric vehicles (via its Gamma Mobility asset-financing brand), alongside earned-wage access, vehicle insurance, health cover, maintenance, and working-capital/micro-credit for independent gig workers. Founded by Kay and Sam out of Africa's e-commerce sector, Gigmile operates across Nigeria and Ghana (Lagos, Accra) and helps mobility entrepreneurs onboard and scale managed fleets of riders.

providers.name: Liazon
providers.description: Liazon was a Buffalo, New York based operator of private benefits exchanges, best known for the Bright Choices Exchange, which helped small and mid-sized employers move to a defined-contribution benefits model and let their employees shop for health, dental, vision, life, and disability coverage through an online marketplace. Backed by Bain Capital Ventures and Bessemer Venture Partners, the company was acquired by Towers Watson — now WTW — and no longer operates as an independent business. As of a 2026-07-19 probe, liazon.com publishes no A record and serves no website over HTTP or HTTPS, while the domain's MX records resolve to willistowerswatson-com.mail.protection.outlook.com and the registration is held through MarkMonitor, indicating WTW retains the domain defensively rather than operating a product on it. There is no Liazon developer portal, documentation, API reference, SDK, or public API surface to catalog. This profile is retained as an acquired-company record; enrichment beyond domain-level DNS evidence is not applicable.

providers.name: Poppins Health
providers.description: Poppins Health is a health insurance provider offering a modern health plan built for small businesses. Headquartered in Ohio, the company focuses on affordability, transparent coverage, and a better member experience for small business owners and their employees. Poppins Health is a portfolio company of the venture firm Anthemis. As of this profile, Poppins Health publishes a public marketing website but does not expose a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation surface for third-party integration.

providers.name: Wagmo
providers.description: Wagmo is a modern pet healthcare company offering three consumer products: Wagmo Wellness (a reimbursement plan covering routine and preventative care such as wellness visits, vaccines, dental cleanings, grooming, and supplements), Wagmo Insurance (accident-and-illness pet insurance for cats and dogs), and VETalk (24/7 virtual televet consultations). Wagmo also distributes its wellness and insurance products as an employee benefit through HR teams and brokers, and partners with pet brands. The company is a Techstars portfolio company. It operates as a direct-to-consumer and B2B2C brand and does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Awork
providers.description: Awork (awork.ge) is a Georgian online job marketplace that connects job seekers with employers across Georgia. The platform lets people search and apply for vacancies directly, while companies post openings and manage their hiring and HR processes digitally. It features an AI assistant named "Argo" that helps users find relevant positions or publish vacancies, and offers native iOS and Android mobile apps alongside the web experience. Awork is backed by 500 Global. The company does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation. Not to be confused with the unrelated German work-management SaaS awork.com, which does operate a developer API.

providers.name: Dechert
providers.description: Dechert LLP is a global law firm founded in 1875 and headquartered in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, with "more than 900 lawyers" across 22 offices in the United States, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia (Wikipedia cites roughly 1,000 attorneys in 20 offices; the firm itself emphasizes a global footprint spanning the U.S., Europe, Asia, and the Middle East). The firm is known for market-leading practices in financial services and investment management, private equity, private credit, mergers and acquisitions, international arbitration, intellectual property, life sciences, white collar enforcement, and antitrust. Dechert publishes deep thought-leadership through its OnPoint series, Crypto Bytes, FSR Radar, THE CRED, and ReTorts; produces multiple podcasts (Dechert 4 Real, Committed Capital, Dechert On Reg); and operates proprietary information platforms including DAMITT (Dechert Antitrust Merger Investigation Timing Tracker), World Compass, World Passport, Dechert Direct, and a Box Portal. Despite these data-driven products, Dechert does not expose any public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI specification, GraphQL endpoint, webhook surface, status page, changelog, or developer portal, and does not publish an RSS feed for OnPoint or any blog series — its only public-facing subscription mechanism is an email preference form.

providers.name: Open
providers.description: Open (Open Financial Technologies) operates at open.money as an India-based fintech offering a connected digital business banking platform for SMEs and startups. It pairs a business current account with invoicing, payments, automated accounting, expense management and payroll, letting founders run their banking and finance operations from a single dashboard. Open is a Speedinvest portfolio company. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; the company website is protected by Cloudflare and no public OpenAPI could be harvested during enrichment.

providers.name: Rumarocket
providers.description: Rumarocket is an AI-powered talent management and HR analytics platform whose tagline is "Hire Talent, Not Employees." It integrates with existing HR systems to synthesize workforce data from hiring through employment, applying machine learning to predict employee attrition and performance, evaluate talent fit for specific roles, and deliver predictive insights for retention and workforce wellness. Backed by 500 Global, the platform exposes user-facing recruitment-algorithm and predictive-insights dashboards but publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or documentation as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: silversheet
providers.description: silversheet was a healthcare credentialing and provider-workforce technology company added to the API Evangelist network as a stub from venture-portfolio sourcing. As of this enrichment pass its domain silversheet.com no longer serves an independent product or developer surface — it redirects to AMN Healthcare's workforce technology platform (amnhealthcare.com/technology/workforce/), indicating the Silversheet brand has been absorbed into AMN Healthcare. No api/developer/docs subdomains resolve, no OpenAPI or developer portal was found, and no first-party API surface exists to enrich. The domain is still administratively live (SPF and DMARC configured, Proofpoint MX), so a domain-security probe was recorded, but there is no independent API to profile.

providers.name: Sprout Wellness Solutions
providers.description: Sprout Wellness Solutions is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of techstars and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Suitable
providers.description: Suitable (Suitable AI) is a talent-acquisition platform that combines AI agents with human expertise to source, screen, and vet engineering and STEM talent for GCCs, AI labs, and innovation centres. Its offering spans a database of technically screened candidates, AI resume screening, and AMPO AI, a conversational AI interviewing agent delivered as AIaaS, across engagement models including contract talent, permanent hires, and executive hiring. As of this enrichment pass Suitable publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or technical documentation surface.

providers.name: TechieMatter
providers.description: TechieMatter is a tech recruitment platform that provides an all-in-one solution to source, filter, assess, interview, and onboard technical talent from around the globe. The platform spans candidate sourcing and resume screening, technical skills assessment and coding evaluations, expert-led technical interviews, and remote-worker onboarding (payroll, compliance, and legal). It serves 900+ companies across 13+ countries, sourcing candidates from 9+ countries across 60+ technical roles including software engineers, data scientists, DevOps, security, product, and hardware roles. No public API or developer platform is documented at this time; this profile is maintained as an API Evangelist network company record.

providers.name: Alight
providers.description: Alight is a leading cloud-based human capital and technology services provider that powers confident health, wealth, and wellbeing decisions for millions of employees and family members. The company delivers integrated benefits administration, payroll, and total wellbeing solutions through its Alight Worklife platform. Alight does not publish a public, self-service developer portal; integrations are typically delivered through enterprise client engagements.

providers.name: Alassio
providers.description: Alassio is a French financial-technology company building a next-generation payroll software platform (logiciel de paie nouvelle generation) for businesses. Alassio positions itself as offering the functional depth expected of a specialist payroll and HR tool, with added transparency and control for finance and people teams. The company is backed by venture-capital firm Partech and operates from France, serving the French and European payroll, compensation, and human-resources market. As of this profile the company publishes only a marketing landing page and a legal notice; no public API, developer documentation, SDK, or integration surface has been located. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub awaiting a public developer surface to enrich.

providers.name: Ally
providers.description: Ally.io was an OKR and goal-management SaaS platform for people and performance teams, helping organizations set, align, and track objectives and key results across the workforce. Backed by Accel, Greylock, Tiger Global and Addition, the company was acquired by Microsoft in October 2021 and its product was folded into Microsoft Viva Goals. The ally.io domain remains actively hosted but no longer exposes a public developer/API surface; developer, docs and API subdomains do not resolve. This API Evangelist profile is retained as an hr-tech portfolio lead with a probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: AllyO
providers.description: AllyO is an HR-tech company, founded in 2016 in Palo Alto, California, that built a conversation-first, AI recruiting chatbot and automation platform for high-volume hiring. Its chatbot let candidates apply to jobs, answer common questions, get screened, and schedule interviews via text and web chat 24/7, with integrations into applicant tracking systems, job boards, and background-check providers. AllyO raised roughly $64M in venture funding (including a $45M round in 2019 backed by investors such as Sapphire Ventures) before being acquired by HireVue in October 2020. The AllyO product now lives inside HireVue as its Conversational AI and Automation offering; www.allyo.com 301-redirects to HireVue and AllyO no longer operates an independent public developer or API surface. This profile is retained as an acquired-company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: andjaro
providers.description: Andjaro is a French SaaS platform for replacement management and workforce flexibility, helping organizations handle short-notice absences, staff shortages, and operational continuity across the private and public sectors. The product gives HR and operations teams real-time visibility of available personnel across an employment ecosystem, matches available workers (CDI/CDD employees, freelancers, and temps) to urgent replacement needs, and automates the administrative workflow by integrating with payroll, ERP, planning, and HRIS systems. It serves facility management, healthcare and social services, the public sector, retail, collective catering, and transport and logistics. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of balderton-capital; no public API, developer portal, or SDK was found during enrichment.

providers.name: atSpoke
providers.description: atSpoke was a modern workplace service desk / internal helpdesk SaaS (formerly askSpoke) that let teams triage and resolve employee support requests across HR, IT, and operations. It was a portfolio company of Accel and was acquired by Okta in August 2021 for approximately $90M to seed Okta's identity governance (IGA) roadmap. The standalone atSpoke product and its entire domain footprint have since been sunset: atspoke.com, askspoke.com, help.atspoke.com and the former public API host api.askspoke.com/api/v1 no longer resolve or serve. This profile is retained as a historical network record; there is no live developer surface left to enrich.

providers.name: Boss
providers.description: Boss (BOSS Zhipin / BOSS直聘) is the largest online recruitment platform in China by average monthly active users, operated by Kanzhun Limited (NASDAQ: BZ, HKEX: 2076) and founded in 2014 in Beijing. It pioneered the "Direct Recruitment" model, a mobile-native experience that connects employers (bosses) and job seekers through instant direct chat rather than static resume exchange, with candidate and job matching powered by proprietary AI algorithms and big-data insights. The consumer job-search product at zhipin.com does not publish a public developer/job-data API; an authorized enterprise developer surface (BossHi mini-program open platform) exists for partners. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of hongshan and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: Bravado
providers.description: Bravado is a community platform for sales professionals, best known as the War Room, which it describes as the world's largest online sales community with more than 400,000 members. Founded in 2016 and headquartered in San Francisco, Bravado offers career networking, anonymous peer Q&A, a jobs and hiring marketplace that matches sales talent with companies, an AI recruiter called Hunter, and a virtual "commission points" rewards currency, delivered through the web and a mobile app. The company is backed by Redpoint Ventures. Bravado does not publish a public developer API; its product is built on an internal GraphQL backend. As of this profile's enrichment date the primary domain bravado.co resolves to a Gandi parking page ("this domain name is unavailable") and is not serving the live product.

providers.name: CenterForce Technologies
providers.description: CenterForce Technologies was a Bethesda, Maryland software company that built workforce-optimization, workforce-management, and performance-analytics software for contact centers. It partnered with Concerto Software for nearly a decade before Concerto acquired it on 2004-04-26 to pair CenterForce's workforce and contact-center management tools with Concerto's ACD, IVR, and email contact-channel products. Concerto was itself taken private in 2005 and rebranded as Aspect Software in 2007, absorbing the former CenterForce workforce-optimization product line. The company raised roughly $6.01M; investors included Battery Ventures, Piper Sandler, Aspect Software, and SightLine Partners. It surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a Battery Ventures portfolio lead. Enrichment (2026-07-18) confirmed it is a long-defunct, acquired entity with no independent website, developer portal, or API surface; there is nothing to catalog.

providers.name: Circular
providers.description: Circular was a Spanish hiring community that connected tech recruiters with software developers, describing itself as a "Hiring Community for Tech Recruiters & Developers." It operated a referral-driven talent network in which recruiters shared vetted candidates they could not place themselves, and developers received job opportunities through that trusted pool rather than through cold outreach. The company was backed by Point Nine Capital and ran its candidate and recruiter landing experiences on a Next.js application served from circular.io and static.circular.io. Circular has since shut down and merged into Manfred (getmanfred.com), the largest tech community in Spain, with its own migration notice stating "Circular cierra sus puertas para integrarse en Manfred." The circular.io domain remains registered to Singular People Europe S.L. but has been fully undelegated, and Point Nine no longer lists Circular in its portfolio. Circular never published a public developer program, API, SDK, or specification. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Clustree
providers.description: Clustree was a French HR-technology startup founded in 2014 that built an AI-powered skills engine and a multilingual skills ontology (over 53,000 verified skills consolidated from more than one billion job skills) used to match employees to internal roles and mobility opportunities. It was acquired by Cornerstone OnDemand in early 2020 (approximately $18.5M, all-cash) and its technology was folded into Cornerstone's People Intelligence / Skills platform. The independent Clustree brand is discontinued: clustree.com no longer serves a website and there is no live developer portal, public API, documentation, SDK, or package registry presence under the Clustree name. This profile is retained as a network identity/lead record only.

providers.name: Crew32
providers.description: Crew32 was a stealth-stage technology startup based in Santa Monica, California, working in the human resources, employment, and workplace-culture space. It was founded by Jason Nazar (previously co-founder and CEO of Docstoc), George Ishii (co-founder of Betterworks, Geni, and Yammer), and Yadid Ramot, and raised roughly $5.8 million in early funding around 2016. The company is publicly associated with the comparably.com workplace-culture and compensation review platform. Crew32 was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as a company lead; no public API, developer portal, or SDK has been identified for this company.

providers.name: CubeTree
providers.description: CubeTree was an enterprise social collaboration software startup (founded 2008, Redwood City, California) offering a business social network with wikis, blogs, file sharing, and activity feeds. It was acquired by SuccessFactors in 2010 (deal valued up to $50M) and folded into the SuccessFactors Business Alignment suite; SAP subsequently acquired SuccessFactors in 2012 and the product was absorbed into SAP SuccessFactors / SAP Jam. CubeTree no longer operates as an independent company: the cubetree.com domain is parked under SAP nameservers with no live web presence, developer portal, documentation, or API. Surfaced as a trinity-ventures portfolio company; retained as a historical/defunct network record with no enrichable API surface.

providers.name: Cultivate
providers.description: Cultivate was an AI-powered digital leadership and coaching platform that analyzed leaders' own opt-in digital communication data to deliver hyper-personalized, privacy-preserving coaching insights and recommendations for people managers. Founded through an Entrepreneur in Residence program at Samsung NEXT by Joseph Freed, Samir Meghani, and Andy Horng, and backed by Trinity Ventures, Silicon Valley Data Capital, and Bloomberg Beta, Cultivate was acquired by employee listening and people-analytics company Perceptyx on February 15, 2022, where it became the basis for Perceptyx's "Cultivate Intelligent Coaching" product. Cultivate operated as an enterprise HR/leadership SaaS and did not publish a public developer API or OpenAPI. This profile is retained as a portfolio-lead record; the company no longer exists as an independent entity.

providers.name: Dexterra
providers.description: Dexterra was a mobile workforce management software startup that built a mobile application platform for managing and optimizing field/mobile operations. Backed by Canaan Partners along with New Enterprise Associates, Intel Capital, Motorola Solutions Venture Capital, and Mesirow Financial, the company raised roughly $108M across its rounds. Dexterra was acquired by Antenna Software in June 2009 and no longer operates as an independent entity; it has no active developer program, public API, or developer portal. This profile is retained as a Canaan Partners portfolio lead for network completeness.

providers.name: Drafted
providers.description: Drafted is a network-recruiting and employee-referral platform, founded in 2015 and headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts, and surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a Y Combinator portfolio company. The product helps companies tap their collective network to source, qualify, and hire talent: a Drafted Slackbot delivers weekly intelligent referral recommendations and lets teams submit referrals straight into their ATS from Slack, while NLP, machine learning, and a graph database of the company network extend matching beyond first-degree employee connections to surface higher-quality referrals. Drafted has been used by thousands of companies ranging from startups to large enterprises. This profile was seeded from a VC-portfolio lead; at enrichment time the public web surface (drafted.us) was not serving a live product site and no public API, developer documentation, or specification could be found.

providers.name: Elite Business Ventures
providers.description: Elite Business Ventures, LLC (EBV, ebvinc.com) is a San Diego-based workplace compliance company founded in 2005 that has helped over one million businesses stay compliant with federal and state labor laws and workplace safety regulations. It operates through two primary brands: PosterElite, a white-label labor-law-poster compliance platform embedded by HR, payroll, HCM, PEO, and workforce-management providers under their own brand; and Osha4Less.com, an ecommerce store of affordable OSHA and labor-law compliance products for small businesses. EBV is a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners. The company exposes no public developer API, SDK, MCP server, or documentation surface — partner integration is handled through direct white-label / reseller arrangements rather than a self-service developer program.

providers.name: Endeavor
providers.description: Endeavor was a global sports and entertainment company representing talent and owning and operating events, with subsidiaries including WME, IMG, and UFC. Following the 2024 take-private transaction by Silver Lake and the separation of TKO Group Holdings (UFC and WWE), the remaining talent, media, marketing, and licensing businesses were rebranded as WME Group. This repository tracks Endeavor as a corporate entity; no public developer APIs are currently published.

providers.name: Endeavor Group Holdings
providers.description: Endeavor Group Holdings was a global sports and entertainment company that represented talent, owned and operated events, and provided licensing, marketing, and media services through subsidiaries including WME, IMG, and UFC. Following the 2024 take-private transaction by Silver Lake and the separation of TKO Group Holdings (UFC and WWE), the remaining talent representation, media, marketing, and licensing businesses were rebranded as WME Group, which now operates WME, 160over90, Pantheon Media Group, and IMG Licensing. No public developer APIs are currently published.

providers.name: Folhamatic
providers.description: Folhamatic (IOB Folhamatic Group) is a Brazilian developer of integrated accounting, payroll, and fiscal/tax software for accounting firms and businesses, founded in 1990 and headquartered in Americana, Sao Paulo. Its product line includes Folhamatic Payroll for personnel management and electronic files, Electronic Point Control for time-clock management, the Folhamatic Accounting system for management reporting, and Folhamatic Written Tax for tax departments. At acquisition it served more than 11,000 companies with 500-plus employees. Folhamatic was acquired by the UK's Sage Group in June 2012 and now operates as part of Sage in Brazil. The company publishes no first-party public developer API, and the historic folhamatic.com.br domain no longer serves a live site.

providers.name: Getlinks
providers.description: GetLinks is an AI-powered hiring operating system for Southeast Asia, operating across Thailand, Singapore, and Vietnam. For employers it provides job posting, AI-driven candidate screening, structured interview tooling with video/audio scoring, and recruiter consulting services; for job seekers it offers job search (14,200+ active jobs in Thailand), salary intelligence sourced from real placements, AI CV readiness analysis, and mock interview training. Backed by 500 Global. No public developer API, SDK, or developer portal was found; the platform is an end-user recruitment and career product.

providers.name: Glintinc
providers.description: Glint (Glint Inc), founded in 2013 and headquartered in Redwood City, California, built a people-success and employee-engagement platform centered on frequent pulse surveys, engagement analytics, and manager action-planning to help organizations measure and improve employee experience. LinkedIn acquired Glint in November 2018, and the product was subsequently folded into Microsoft Viva as Viva Glint. There is no standalone Glint developer portal or public API: the former glintinc.com domain now 302-redirects to Microsoft's Viva Glint community, and the offering is delivered and documented through Microsoft Viva. This profile is retained for network lineage as a Norwest Venture Partners portfolio company that was acquired rather than an independently operating API provider.

providers.name: Glints
providers.description: Glints is a talent recruitment and career development platform headquartered in Singapore and operating across Southeast Asia, including Indonesia, Vietnam, Malaysia, Taiwan and the Philippines. Founded in 2013, it runs an online job marketplace connecting job seekers with employers, a curated headhunting service (TalentHunt), and a cross-border managed-talent / remote-hiring offering that lets companies build and employ distributed teams across the region. Glints also publishes career resources and expert classes. It is one of the largest talent ecosystems in Southeast Asia and is backed by investors including DCM Ventures, Monk's Hill Ventures and PERSOL. This API Evangelist profile was added as a portfolio-company lead; Glints exposes no public developer API at this time.

providers.name: GoDays
providers.description: GoDays is an AI-powered workforce analytics platform for enterprises that predicts and helps prevent employee burnout. It analyzes internal company data — keyboard usage behaviors, employee sentiment, interactions, performance, and feedback — to measure and forecast burnout risk, then surfaces recommendations to improve workflow, productivity, and employee wellbeing. Founded in 2021 and based in Seoul (Gangnam), South Korea, the company was co-founded by CEO Yelnur Kai and Adiar Bopov, and raised a seed round in 2024 with participation from 500 Global and Domino VC. GoDays was added to the API Evangelist network as a 500 Global portfolio company; as of this enrichment pass it publishes a marketing site only, with no public API, developer portal, or specification surface.

providers.name: Good & Co.
providers.description: Good & Co. (Good&Co Labs, Inc.) was a Techstars-backed startup that built a research-driven psychometric and culture-fit platform for hiring and employee engagement, using Big Five-based personality assessments to match candidates, teammates, and workplaces via a proprietary FitScore. As of this enrichment pass the original company appears defunct with no live developer or API surface, and the good.co domain now resolves to an unrelated third-party logistics (3PL) fulfillment business.

providers.name: HomeJoy
providers.description: Homejoy, Inc. was an online home-services marketplace that connected customers with vetted house cleaners and handymen through its website and mobile apps. Founded in 2010 by siblings Adora and Aaron Cheung, the Y Combinator-backed company raised roughly $40M (Google Ventures, Redpoint, First Round, Max Levchin) and expanded to more than 30 cities across the US, UK, Canada, France and Germany. Battered by high customer churn, discount-driven growth and worker-misclassification lawsuits, Homejoy ceased operations on July 31, 2015; much of its product and engineering team was acqui-hired by Google. This is an archival API Evangelist profile of a defunct company: it operates no public API, developer portal, or SDKs, and its former homejoy.com domain now redirects to an unrelated cleaning service.

providers.name: Hyphen
providers.description: Hyphen was a mobile-first employee engagement and pulse-survey platform that let organizations collect anonymous employee feedback, run continuous sentiment surveys, and give managers analytics on engagement and culture. Founded as a 500 Global-backed startup, Hyphen was acquired by Betterworks and folded into the Betterworks Engage product line. Its original domain, gethyphen.com, now 301-redirects to betterworks.com/product/engage-overview/, and the company no longer operates an independent public developer or API surface. This profile is retained as an acquired-company lead in the API Evangelist network; the live successor product is Betterworks Engage.

providers.name: iMedeon
providers.description: iMedeon, Inc. was a mobile workforce management software company based in Atlanta, Georgia, providing wireless web applications to optimize scheduling, routing, and the dispatch and management of mobile field workforces (the iM:Work suite). It was acquired by ViryaNet Ltd. in February 2002 (later rolled into Verisae) and no longer operates independently. The domain imedeon.com does not resolve and there is no live website, developer portal, or API surface. Retained in the API Evangelist network as a defunct/legacy company profile; there is nothing to enrich.

providers.name: Jibe
providers.description: Jibe was an HR-tech / talent-acquisition and recruitment-marketing SaaS company, surfaced as a portfolio company of sapphire-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass the company no longer operates independently: its domain www.jibe.com issues a blanket HTTP 301 redirect to www.icims.com (Jibe was acquired by iCIMS), and no independent Jibe developer portal, API, OpenAPI, or .well-known surface exists to harvest. No API artifacts could be enriched without fabrication.

providers.name: Jopwell
providers.description: Jopwell was a career advancement and diversity-recruiting platform that connected Black, Latinx, and Native American students and professionals with employers for jobs, internships, and career resources. Founded in 2015 and backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and other investors, it was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. As of an enrichment probe on 2026-07-19, the jopwell.com domain returns an HTTP 301 redirect to trueplatform.com (True, an executive search and talent-management firm), indicating the standalone Jopwell product is no longer operating. No public developer program, API, OpenAPI specification, documentation, or /.well-known/security.txt surface was found, so no API artifacts could be produced.

providers.name: Kelly Services
providers.description: Kelly Services is a global leader in providing workforce solutions, connecting talented people to companies in need of their skills across a variety of industries including staffing, talent management, and outsourcing.

providers.name: Koru Careers
providers.description: Koru (joinkoru.com) was a Seattle-based predictive hiring and people-analytics SaaS company. Its platform built a per-employer "predictive hiring fingerprint" and scored candidates against the Koru7 Impact Skills assessment — Grit, Rigour, Impact, Teamwork, Curiosity, Ownership and Polish — via a 20-minute online pre-interview that produced a Candidate Fit Score, with the stated goal of increasing quality of hire and reducing screening bias. Products were marketed as Koru Hire and Koru Develop. The company was acquired by Cappfinity: between February and November 2020 joinkoru.com began redirecting to koru.cappfinity.com, where the Koru7 Impact Skills Assessment was carried as a Cappfinity product. That subdomain now redirects to cappfinity.com, which carries no remaining Koru branding, and the joinkoru.com domain has lapsed and currently serves unrelated online-gambling affiliate content. Koru published no public developer portal, documentation, or API; this profile is retained as a historical record of a defunct company and no live endpoints are catalogued.

providers.name: Likeplum
providers.description: Likeplum (likeplum.com) was an online expert-knowledge and task marketplace that billed itself as "expert knowledge and skills at your fingertips" and invited users to "ask experts to answer your questions and hire skilled engineers, programmers, designers, writers, marketers and more on the world's largest information trading marketplace." Members posted either a free-to-ask question or a paid task, received answers and completed work from the site's expert pool, and paid only after approving the result under a post-pay model, with optional fully private posts and card or PayPal settlement. Its busiest categories were writing, programming, graphic design, and marketing and SEO. By late 2014 the company had folded the brand into the "Createpool" network, splitting its four most popular categories into dedicated sites — hackerpool.com for programming tasks, studypool.com for academic and homework Q&A, mechanicpool.com for auto repair, and counselpool.com for legal questions — and migrated every likeplum account, question, answer, and profile across. Only the academic property survives today: likeplum.com now 301-redirects to www.studypool.com, while createpool.com fails TLS negotiation and hackerpool.com, mechanicpool.com, and counselpool.com no longer resolve. The Likeplum brand exposes no developer portal, documentation, SDK, package, or public API, so this profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as an identity record for a rebranded 500 Global portfolio company rather than as an API provider.

providers.name: Lytmus
providers.description: Lytmus was a technical-interview and coding-assessment platform for hiring engineers. Candidates worked live in a browser-based, fully functional Ubuntu virtual machine (Terminal, editors, Chrome) so recruiters could run pair-programming phone screens and evaluate real coding skills across languages and full-stack scenarios, priced in per-session plans. Surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead. Enrichment probing (2026-07-20) found no developer portal, API, documentation, or ./.well-known surface; the company was acquired by GitHub in 2019 and its product has since been shut down, so lytmus.io now serves stale content and lytmus.com is a parked, for-sale domain. No API artifacts exist to enrich.

providers.name: Maimai
providers.description: Maimai (脉脉) is a Chinese professional networking and workplace social platform operated by Beijing Taoyou Tianxia Technology Development Co., Ltd. It combines professional networking, recruitment and talent matching, job referrals, company reviews and workplace community, and career-development learning (脉课堂) for the Chinese-language market. Surfaced as a portfolio company of dcm-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Maimai publishes no public developer program, open platform, or API documentation, so this profile carries identity and domain-security signals only.

providers.name: Manpower
providers.description: Manpower is a global workforce solutions brand of ManpowerGroup that delivers innovative staffing and workforce services to organizations worldwide and helps talent find meaningful, sustainable employment. No public developer APIs have been documented.

providers.name: ManpowerGroup
providers.description: ManpowerGroup is a global workforce solutions company that connects talented people with innovative companies through its family of brands including Manpower, Experis, and Talent Solutions. No public developer APIs have been documented.

providers.name: Mayflower
providers.description: Mayflower is an early-stage (Y Combinator, Fall 2025) startup building an AI-powered HR plug-in that automates immigration screening, visa eligibility assessment, and compliance for international hiring. The platform parses candidate documents, classifies visa pathways, and generates attorney-ready forms, integrating directly with existing HR systems so companies can surface only compliant candidates and reduce legal risk. Founded in 2025 by Naren Chittem and Aryan Gulati and based in San Francisco, the company currently operates a marketing landing page with a book-a-call motion and publishes no public API, developer documentation, SDKs, or GitHub organization. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a Y Combinator portfolio lead; the enrichment pipeline found no API surface to harvest.

providers.name: Mya Systems
providers.description: Mya Systems was a San Francisco based HR-tech company, founded in 2012 by Eyal Grayevsky and James Maddox, that built Mya, a conversational-AI recruiting assistant automating candidate outreach, screening, scheduling and communications across the hiring lifecycle, integrating with major ATS, CRM and HRIS platforms such as Workday and SAP SuccessFactors. Backed by Emergence Capital, the company was acquired by The StepStone Group (Totaljobs) in May 2021, when its founders and engineering team joined StepStone; the standalone mya.com and hiremya.com developer, product and API surfaces are retired and mya.com now redirects to thestepstonegroup.com. No independent public API, developer portal or machine-readable specification remains for Mya Systems.

providers.name: NodeFlair
providers.description: NodeFlair is a Singapore-based technology career-transparency platform, founded in 2018 by Ethan Ang, that gives Asia's tech talent access to verified salary data, company reviews, tech-stack insights, benefits, and job listings across the APAC region. Salaries are verified against actual employee payslips, differentiating NodeFlair from other job boards, and the platform serves over 500,000 monthly visitors across eight Asian countries while helping companies hire tech talent. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. No public developer API surface was found during enrichment; the profile currently carries live domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Open Skills
providers.description: Job titles, skills and related jobs data

providers.name: Orgspace
providers.description: Orgspace, Inc. was a B2B people-operations software company offering org design, staffing, and workforce analytics tools that integrated alongside existing HR/HRIS systems. Its product let teams create team configurations, propose org charts, visualize cost projections, and build headcount plans framed around assigning people into roles rather than tracking open positions. Surfaced as a portfolio company of bloomberg-beta and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead. As of this enrichment pass the orgspace.io domain no longer resolves (no DNS records) and the company appears defunct; no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or documentation surface could be found.

providers.name: Pento
providers.description: Pento was a European (UK/Danish) automated payroll platform that let companies run payroll, sync with accounting and HR tools, and pay employees in a few clicks; it was backed by Point Nine and Seedcamp. As of this enrichment pass the pento.io domain (HTTP 301) redirects to HiBob (www.hibob.com) and serves HiBob's HR-software marketing site with no remaining Pento branding, indicating Pento's payroll product has been folded into HiBob. There is no independent Pento developer program, API, or documentation surface to enrich; any live payroll API now lives under HiBob. This profile is retained as a network lead with its acquisition/redirect status recorded.

providers.name: Platypus
providers.description: Platypus is a Danish HR-technology company (a Speedinvest portfolio company, invested 2019) that built a talent lifecycle management solution for HR managers. Its people-analytics product helped HR professionals measure what employees value at every stage of the talent lifecycle - from attraction through management to retention - using a value-centric approach to company culture built on 12 work-related values across 3 core areas of organizational culture, surfacing individual needs and priorities while protecting employee anonymity. No public API, developer portal, OpenAPI, or other machine-readable API surface was found during enrichment; the company's former domains (getplatypus.com, platypus.ai) are now parked / listed for sale, indicating the product appears to be inactive/defunct.

providers.name: Plerk
providers.description: Plerk was a Mexican fintech startup offering an employee-benefits and perks platform ("beneficios para colaboradores") for companies in Mexico, backed by 500 Global. During 2023 Plerk merged with minu to consolidate the employee benefits offering in Mexico, and the standalone Plerk product was wound down. Its primary domain plerk.com no longer resolves (DNS fully lapsed; last web archive May 2023) and plerk.io redirects to the now-defunct plerk.com. Support was handled at soporte@plerk.io. This profile is retained as a defunct/acquired lead; the surviving product and any API surface live under minu. No live developer portal, API, SDK, or documentation surface exists for Plerk.

providers.name: Qapa
providers.description: Qapa (qapa.fr) is a Paris-based French online recruitment and temporary-work (interim) marketplace that matched companies with job seekers for permanent and temp placements. Backed by Index Ventures and Partech, it was majority-acquired by the Adecco Group. The qapa.fr web property is now gated behind an Azure Application Gateway (HTTP 403) and exposes no public developer, API, or documentation surface; this profile is retained as an API Evangelist network record.

providers.name: Qerja
providers.description: PT Qerja Manfaat Bangsa (Qerja) is an Indonesian human-resources company operating an end-to-end HR product ecosystem for employers, established in 2007 and later part of the PT M Cash Integrasi Tbk technology group. In 2019 it acquired Karir.com, Indonesia's first job portal (since 1998), and reports serving over 50,000 clients and 8 million member users across the country. The public presence is a corporate marketing site (qerjagroup.com) covering its HR services, clients, and user demographics; no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Raised
providers.description: Raised (joinraised.com) is an AI-powered recruiting platform founded in 2022 and backed by 500 Global. It delivers vetted candidates to venture-backed startups — particularly in AI, deep tech, and Web3 — at a fraction of the cost and time of traditional recruitment agencies, using proprietary AI to match candidates to roles. The company is headquartered in Wilmington, Delaware, and operates as a software-enabled alternative to traditional staffing firms. Raised publishes a marketing website only; no public developer API, documentation, or developer platform surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: RolePoint
providers.description: RolePoint was an employee referral, internal mobility, and talent-acquisition software company that helped recruitment teams source, refer, and redeploy talent through referral programs and internal mobility marketplaces, with a "Connect" API layer for integrating into ATS/HRIS systems such as iCIMS. The company was acquired by Jobvite in 2019 and folded into the Jobvite Talent Acquisition Suite; the standalone rolepoint.com domain no longer resolves and no independent developer portal or API surface remains reachable. It is tracked here as a 500 Global portfolio company.

providers.name: ShearShare
providers.description: ShearShare is a B2B2C marketplace that lets salon and barbershop owners rent out unused chairs, booths, and suites to licensed beauty and barbering professionals on a flexible, on-demand basis — space-as-a-service for the hair, beauty, and grooming industry. Through its mobile app and web platform, independent stylists, barbers, and cosmetologists discover and book professional space by the day, while shop owners monetize idle capacity. Founded in 2015 by Dr. Tye Caldwell and Courtney Caldwell and headquartered in McKinney, Texas, the company has been featured on ABC's Shark Tank and is backed by 500 Global among other investors.

providers.name: Skillbridge
providers.description: Skillbridge (skillbridge.co) was a New York-based online marketplace for freelance consultants and independent professionals, connecting organizations from Fortune 500 companies to early-stage startups with vetted specialists for short-term engagements. Founded in 2013, it was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a 500 Global portfolio company. Skillbridge was acquired by Toptal in 2016 and folded into what became Toptal Business; the skillbridge.co domain now 301-redirects to toptal.com/finance. The company operates no independent developer API, documentation, developer portal, SDKs, or event surface, so there are no technical artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: SnapShyft
providers.description: SnapShyft is an on-demand staffing marketplace that connects hospitality, food-and-beverage, and events venues with vetted gig workers for short-notice shifts. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass its primary domain (snapshyft.com) serves a coming-soon placeholder page and exposes no public API, developer portal, documentation, changelog, or /.well-known discovery surface. The only machine-verifiable signal harvested was domain/transport security (TLS 1.3, HSTS, DMARC quarantine); the profile remains a lead awaiting a live developer surface.

providers.name: SpringRole
providers.description: SpringRole was a blockchain-based professional reputation and attestation platform — an endorsement and verified-resume network that let people attest to each other's skills and work history on-chain — and was a portfolio company of Bloomberg Beta. Its primary domain, springrole.com, now issues a 301 redirect to Springworks (springworks.in), an HR-technology company whose products include SpringVerify (background verification), Goodfit (AI-native recruitment), and EngageWith (employee engagement). An enrichment pass on 2026-07-21 found no public developer API, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, developer portal, SDK/package, MCP server, llms.txt, or /.well-known discovery documents for SpringRole (the well-known paths return the Webflow marketing SPA, not real artifacts), and no separate developer or docs subdomain resolves.

providers.name: Surfboard
providers.description: Surfboard (teamsurfboard.com) was a workforce management (WFM) SaaS for customer support teams — scheduling, forecasting, and real-time staffing for contact centers — backed by Seedcamp and Speedinvest. As of this enrichment pass the standalone product no longer operates independently; teamsurfboard.com returns an HTTP 301 permanent redirect to Dialpad's workforce management software page (dialpad.com/features/workforce-management-software), indicating Surfboard was acquired by / folded into Dialpad. No standalone Surfboard developer portal, API reference, or OpenAPI surface is publicly reachable; all probed /.well-known/ discovery endpoints return 404.

providers.name: Syft
providers.description: Syft (originally Syft Online Ltd, later branded "Syft by Indeed") is a UK-founded flexible-staffing marketplace launched in London in 2015 by Jack Beaman and Novo Abakare. Its platform connects employers across hospitality, retail, industrial, care and facilities-management directly with vetted, rated temporary and part-time workers, removing the traditional recruitment agency and charging a flat fee on top of worker wages. Creandum led Syft's Series A in 2017; the company was acquired by Indeed in 2019 and now operates as part of Indeed Flex. Syft is a consumer/employer staffing marketplace and exposes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Talentpluto
providers.description: Talentpluto (Pluto) is an AI voice-agent platform for professional discovery and recruitment, founded in 2025 and part of Y Combinator's Summer 2026 batch out of New York City. Professionals talk to Pluto for about ten minutes about what they have done, what they are great at, and what they want next; Pluto turns that private conversation into a discoverable professional profile that the person controls and that can be shared with people and AI agents. For hiring, companies describe what they need and Pluto searches its network and the broader market, evaluates fit on both sides, privately confirms interest, and facilitates warm introductions when there is mutual alignment. The company positions Pluto as a source of truth for career context in an internet increasingly built for agents. As of profiling it is a consumer- and recruiter-facing product with no public developer API, SDK, documentation portal, or other machine-facing surface; this profile is a network stub awaiting a real API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Tapchief
providers.description: Tapchief was an India-based online marketplace that connected businesses and professionals with a vetted network of freelance experts, consultants, and advisors for project-based work, on-demand consultations, and expert advice. Founded in Bengaluru and backed by 500 Startups (500 Global), the platform let companies discover, book, and collaborate with independent talent across functions such as marketing, finance, product, and technology. Tapchief was acquired by Chargebee in 2021, and the tapchief.com domain is now dormant. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead; probing found no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Teamnote
providers.description: TeamNote is an enterprise mobile productivity and secure communication platform founded in Hong Kong in 2014 and part of Y Combinator's Winter 2015 batch. Positioned as "Slack for mobile workforces," it gives corporations a mobile-first workspace for team messaging, collaboration, workflow forms, announcements, and content distribution to frontline and deskless staff, with enterprise security and administration controls. The product originally shipped at teamnoteapp.com (its first customer was Cheung Kong Holdings) and the company now presents at teamnote.ai. No public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or documentation surface was discoverable during enrichment; both web properties are bot-protected.

providers.name: VNDLY
providers.description: VNDLY is a cloud-based vendor management system (VMS) for managing contingent workforce, external labor, statements of work (SOW), and services procurement. Founded in 2017 and headquartered in Mason, Ohio, VNDLY was acquired by Workday in 2021 and is now offered as Workday VNDLY, pairing with Workday Human Capital Management (HCM) for total workforce optimization. The company no longer operates an independent public developer portal or API surface; integration is delivered through the Workday platform. This profile originated as a portfolio-company lead (Battery Ventures, Insight Partners) surfaced into the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Walzay Inc.
providers.description: Walzay Inc. is a global tech-talent recruitment marketplace, founded in 2019 by Humaira Khan and headquartered in New York City. The platform connects companies with vetted remote and in-office software, engineering, and sales professionals — largely sourced from the Middle East and other emerging markets — and offers white-glove recruiting alongside a self-serve candidate marketplace. Walzay is backed by 500 Global and the Sanabil 500 MENA Seed Accelerator. No public API or developer surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Wanted
providers.description: Wanted was a talent-sourcing recruitment marketplace, backed by Partech and founded by Jean Meyer, that set out to disrupt traditional headhunting by connecting companies with candidates surfaced and referred through a networked marketplace. It operated out of New York and France under the Applicative SaaS / HR-tech category. The company has since wound down: its team was acqui-hired by Revolut, and the product and website at getwanted.com are no longer live (the domain is now parked and listed for sale on HugeDomains). No public API, developer portal, SDKs, or documentation could be found for this provider. This profile is retained as a historical company record; there is no live API surface to enrich.

providers.name: WorkClass
providers.description: WorkClass is (or was) a Singapore-based job marketplace founded in 2020 that matched frontline and blue-collar workers with employers, promising placement within 24 hours via matching algorithms. Backed by 500 Global, Goodwater Capital, Antler, and Kistefos, it surfaced here as a 500 Global portfolio lead. As of July 2026 its primary domain workclass.co redirects to an unrelated UK website and workclass.com is parked for sale; no public API, developer portal, client packages, or GitHub organization were found.

providers.name: Zugata
providers.description: Zugata was a San Francisco-based continuous performance-management and peer-feedback SaaS company, backed by Canaan Partners and others. Its platform let employees give and receive real-time, skill-based feedback and driver-of-performance insights for coaching and reviews. Culture Amp acquired Zugata in 2019 and folded its peer-feedback capabilities into the Culture Amp employee-experience platform; the standalone Zugata product and website (zugata.com) have since been retired. The domain still resolves NS and Proofpoint MX records (email routing) but serves no website, developer portal, documentation, or public API. No API surface exists to enrich — this profile is retained as a historical portfolio-company record.

providers.name: Smalt
providers.description: Smalt is a Berlin-based training academy and technology platform for the green-energy installation trades. It combines a B2B installation services business (solar and, increasingly, heat pumps and other climate-trade work) with an education platform that upskills and certifies installers, plus a franchise model that lets trained installers run their own training businesses on Smalt's learning materials and tooling. Founded in 2023 and backed by General Catalyst, noa, Owl Ventures, Heartfelt, La Famiglia and Loric Ventures, Smalt is a workforce/services company rather than an API provider; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI, or SDK surface to catalog.
